> Due to required system maintenance, there will be impacts to in\-person transactions at UBC Sport Facilities on Wednesday, May 27 from 8:00am – 5:00pm\. [Read more\.](https://recreation.ubc.ca/2026/05/25/in-person-reg-rentals-bookings-limited-may-27/)

Drop\-in ice at the Doug Mitchell Thunderbird Sports Centre provides an easy way to be physically active, and participants of all skill levels are welcome to participate**\.** 

Participants can choose from the following ice sessions: public skating, figure skating, drop\-in hockey, family hockey and stick & puck\. Drop\-in sessions are scheduled throughout the year, and can be viewed below in the drop\-in sports schedule\.

***Please note that the schedules are subject to change** due to unexpected circumstances and we encourage you to bookmark and reference this schedule prior to any visit\. In the event of an unscheduled closure this calendar is the first place that we update\.*

### Online Reservations & Drop\-In Access

All activities require reservations using the online registration system\. These sessions help ensure entry to visitors during peak periods\.

-   **REGISTER – Online registration is required\.** If capacity permits walk\-in guests, they will be asked to complete their booking using the online registration\. Reservations are available up to 48 hours prior to each session start time\. Please do not arrive more than 10 minutes before the scheduled time\.
-   **DROP\-IN** – Entry is first\-come, first\-serve and subject to venue capacity\.

### Activities

| Activity | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| [**Family Hockey**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/ice/drop-in-ice/#family-hockey) | These sessions require full hockey equipment and may include skaters as young as 6\. Games, scrimmages, and practice are not permitted\. |
| [**Figure Skating**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/ice/drop-in-ice/#figure-skating) | Figure Skating sessions are for skaters who want to work on their jumps, spins, and on\-ice routines\. Figure skaters may practice jumps and spins in the centre area of the ice but no full ice routines\. |
| [**Hockey**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/ice/drop-in-ice/#hockey) | Sessions are intended for full\-sheet, informal, and unofficiated games of hockey\.  Line changes on the fly and pinnies provided\. Full hockey gear is required\. **Goalie registration is free \(call 604\.827\.4324 on session date to register\)\.** |
| [**Public Skating**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/ice/drop-in-ice/#public-skating) | Public skating sessions are for skaters of all abilities and for lap skating only\. Wheelchairs and strollers permitted\. |
| [**Stick & Puck**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/ice/drop-in-ice/#stick-puck) | Stick & Puck sessions are intended for individual work on skating, stickhandling, shooting, and passing skills\. Scrimmages, games, and team training are not permitted\. |

*Additional rules apply for each activity\. Please review rules and etiquette for each activity prior to your next visit\.*

### Rules

-   All participants are required to check in at the Doug Mitchell Thunderbird Sports Centre Pro Shop and wear a wristband \(or pinny\) during the entirety of the drop\-in activity\.
    -   All skaters 17 years of age and younger must have a parent or legal guardian sign a waiver at check\-in\.
-   All skaters 12 years of age and younger must be accompanied by an adult on the ice\.
-   Helmets
    -   CSA\-approved hockey helmets are required for all skaters 12 years of age and younger\.
    -   CSA\-approved hockey helmets are strongly recommended for all skaters\.
    -   Bicycle helmets are not permitted\.
-   Skaters must wait until the Zamboni has left the ice surface and rink doors are closed before entering the ice surface\.
-   Unauthorized coaching and lessons not permitted\.
-   Anyone perceived under the influence of drugs and alcohol will be refused entry
-   All participants skate at their own risk

Family Hockey Rules

-   All skaters are required to wear CSA\-approved hockey helmets\.
-   Skaters 16 years of age and younger are required to wear full hockey equipment\.
-   The following activities and items are not permitted:
    -   Goalies, games, drills, or scrimmages\.
    -   Training devices \(including cones\)\.
    -   Aggressive shooting or slap shots\.
    -   Body checking or unnecessary contact\.
-   A maximum of 30 skaters are permitted on ice at any given time\.

Figure Skating Rules

-   All skaters are required to wear figure skates\.
-   The following activities and items are not permitted:
    -   Games, sticks, pucks, or balls\.
    -   Training devices \(including cones\)\.

Hockey Rules

-   All skaters are required to wear full equipment, including a CSA\-approved hockey helmet\.
-   All skaters must provide government issued, photo ID at check\-in\.
-   The following activities and items are not permitted:
    -   Body checking or unnecessary contact\.
-   A maximum of 26 skaters and 2 goalies are permitted for each session\.

Public Skating Rules

-   All persons on ice are required to wear skates\.
-   The following activities and items are not permitted:
    -   Carrying of children on ice – strollers are permitted\.
    -   Speed skates, jumps, spins, or digging of skates into the ice\.
    -   Dangerous activities such as snowballs, throwing of objects, racing, fast skating, weaving through other skaters, etc\.
    -   Games, sticks, pucks, or balls\.
    -   Food or beverages on ice\.

Stick & Puck Rules

-   All skaters are required to wear CSA\-approved hockey helmets\.
-   Skaters 16 years of age and younger are required to wear full hockey equipment\.
-   The following activities and items are not permitted:
    -   Goalies, games, drills, or scrimmages\.
    -   Training devices \(including cones\)\.
    -   Aggressive shooting or slap shots\.
    -   Body checking or unnecessary contact\.
-   A maximum of 30 skaters are permitted on ice at any given time\.

### Hockey & Skate Rentals

Skate and helmet rentals are available for rent from the Doug Mitchell Thunderbird Sports Centre Pro Shop\.

title: UBC Tennis Coaches
content_markdown:
[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/JJ-cropped-150x150.jpg)

JJ Mahony

With over 35 years of coaching experience, JJ joined the UBC Tennis Centre in 2011 after serving as Tennis Director at the North Shore Winter Club from 2003 to 2011\. Since arriving at UBC, he has led the program as Tennis Director for more than 15 years, continuing to share his passion for the game with players of all ages and levels\. A highly accomplished competitor, JJ played in junior provincial, national, and international events, and proudly represented Canada at the ITF World Championships in the 35\+ division in New Zealand\. In his current role, JJ oversees all operations at the UBC Tennis Centre and remains dedicated to growing and promoting tennis as a lifelong sport within the community\.

**Experience:**

-   ***Tennis Director*** – UBC Tennis Centre \(2011\-Present\)
-   ***Tennis Director*** – North Shore Winter Club \(2003\-2011\)
-   ***Head Assistant Pro*** – Shaughnessy Golf and Country Club \(2000\-2002\)
-   ***Assistant Pro*** – The Arbutus Club \(1989\-2000\)

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Greg-Macken-Profile-e1774996654310-150x150.png)

Greg Macken

Greg Macken is the Head Coach at the UBC Tennis Centre, where he leads the coaching team and oversees the design and delivery of tennis programs across all age groups and skill levels\. With over 15 years of coaching experience, Greg has worked in a variety of roles focused on program management, coach mentorship, and junior development\.

His coaching background includes experience at the Arbutus Club and St\. George’s School, where he was involved in coaching both recreational and competitive players\. From 2016 to 2022, he served as the Competitive Program Coordinator at UBC Tennis Centre, specializing in junior development and supporting players competing at the provincial level\.

Greg’s approach emphasizes long\-term development, inclusive programming, and fostering a positive learning environment for both athletes and coaches\.

**Experience & Certifications:**

-   ***Head Coach*** *– UBC Tennis Centre \(2022 – Present\)*
-   ***Competitive Program Coordinator*** *– UBC Tennis Centre \(2016 – 2022\)*
-   ***Tennis Coach*** *– UBC Tennis Centre \(2012 – Present\)*
-   ***Tennis Coach*** *– Arbutus Club \(2012 – 2020\)*
-   ***Tennis Coach*** *– St\. George’s School \(2010 – 2014\)*
-   ***UBC Tennis Team*** *\(2014 – 2015\)*
-   ***Course Facilitator –*** *Tennis Canada*
-   ***Club Pro 3 \(in progress\)*** *– Tennis Canada*
-   ***Club Pro 2*** *– Tennis Canada*
-   ***Club Pro 1*** *– Tennis Canada*
-   ***Wheelchair Tennis Certified*** *– Tennis Canada*

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Pete-cropped-150x150.jpg)

Pete Grimsey

Pete Grimsey is the High Performance Director at the UBC Tennis Centre, where he has led one of British Columbia’s top programs since January 2020\. With more than 20 years of coaching experience at public and private clubs in North America, Pete has developed numerous junior athletes from provincial to national levels and helped guide many players to successful NCAA collegiate careers\.

From 2013 to 2019, Pete served as a Provincial Coach with Tennis BC, leading and assisting with training camps as well as travelling with British Columbia’s highest\-ranked junior players to several Canadian National Championships\. He has also travelled with players to the prestigious Little Mo International tournaments in California \(2018\) and Florida \(2019\)\. He has also done contract work for Tennis Canada including a U12 National Training Camp in Montreal and coached Canada’s three top U18 female prospects at the Vancouver ITF J60 tournament in 2019\.

Pete worked as part of Rebecca Marino’s coaching team from 2021 to 2022\. In this role, he assisted with her off\-season training in preparation for 2022 and travelled with her to several tournaments including the 2022 Australian Open where she successfully qualified for the main draw\.

Recognized for his contributions to player development and high\-performance coaching, Pete was awarded the Tennis BC High Performance Coach of the Year in 2016\. He combines an accomplished playing background with extensive coaching experience, bringing a wealth of knowledge and expertise to the UBC Tennis Centre’s High Performance Program\. Pete is passionate about developing athletes both on and off the court and helping them achieve their goals—whether competing at the national level, earning opportunities to play collegiate tennis, or pursuing a professional career\.

**Experience and Certifications**

-   **High Performance Director** – UBC Tennis Centre \(2020–Present\)
-   **WTA Tour Travelling Coach** – Rebecca Marino \(2021–2022\)
-   **Tennis BC Provincial Coach** – U16 Canadian Indoor & Outdoor Championships \(2016–2019\)
-   **Tennis BC Provincial Coach** – U14 Canadian Outdoor National Championships \(2015\)
-   **Tennis Canada Coach** – ITF J60, Vancouver \(2019\)
-   **Tennis Canada Coach** – U12 National Camp, Montreal \(2018\)
-   **Tennis BC Coach** – Little Mo International Tours – California \(2018\) & Florida \(2019\)
-   **Tennis BC Training Camp Coach** \(2013–2019\)
-   **Tennis BC High Performance Coach of The Year** – 2016
-   **Tennis Canada Coach 3 Certification** – Tennis Canada

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Alberto-cropped-150x150.jpg)

Alberto Sanchez

Alberto Sanchez, currently serving as the UBC Tennis Centre Coordinator of Competitive Programs, brings a wealth of tennis expertise to his role\. With Club Pro 2 and Coach 3 certifications from Tennis Canada, Alberto’s coaching journey began in Madrid, where he worked as a Tennis and Padel tennis instructor before relocating to Vancouver in 2016\. 

Throughout his career, Alberto has demonstrated a strong commitment to developing tennis programs for players of all ages and skill levels\. He has worked extensively with both kids and adults, fostering a passion for the sport and helping players reach their full potential\. 

In addition to his work at the UBC Tennis Centre, Alberto has served as a provincial tennis coach for Tennis Alberta at U14 Nationals and Tennis BC at U12 Nationals\. He remains actively involved in provincial tennis camps and national competitions, where he continues to mentor and develop young athletes\. 

Alberto’s dedication to the sport extends beyond coaching\. As a Tennis Canada Course facilitator, he contributes to the education and development of future tennis coaches in Canada\. With his extensive experience and passion for tennis, Alberto is committed to providing top\-notch coaching and guidance to all players at the UBC Tennis Centre\.

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/IMG_8629-scaled-e1774996286747-150x150.jpg)

Michelle Linhart

Michelle is a born and raised Vancouverite, having spent 16 years coaching competition rock climbing\. A few years ago, she stumbled upon tennis while looking for a change of scenery and fell in love immediately\. An experienced High\-Performance athlete and coach, Michelle holds a Masters in High Performance Coaching at UBC, bolstering her experience and love for the game of Tennis\.  

Michelle is a Club Pro 2 Certified Coach and oversees UBC Tennis Centre’s Events and Mixers, as well a Students, Staff, Faculty and Seniors Programs\. As a leader at the UBC Tennis Centre, Michelle is looking forward to sharing her love of tennis with players of all ages, levels and backgrounds\.

John brings over 22 years of competitive tennis experience, having played tournaments as a junior across Canada and competed in Junior ITFs in Florida\. He has been coaching for the past five years, beginning his career in Toronto before relocating to BC, where he coached at the Whistler Racket Club\. Now proudly coaching at the UBC Tennis Centre and overseeing UBC’s Junior Development Programs, John is passionate about every facet of the game and is committed to helping players improve and enjoy the sport\. 

Beyond the court, John’s love for the outdoors shines through in his hobbies, which include snowboarding, hiking, and mountain biking\. A dedicated endurance athlete, he also enjoys running and road cycling, always seeking new challenges\.

Thiago Barros is a Tennis Professional at the UBC Tennis Centre with over 25 years of coaching experience across private clubs, tennis academies, and recreational programs in both Brazil and Canada\. His coaching philosophy emphasizes strong technical foundations, fitness integration, and inclusive instruction for players of all ages and levels\.

Since moving to Vancouver, Thiago has contributed to the coaching teams at the Jericho Tennis Club and worked under Gord Haukas Tennis, developing and leading lessons focused on skill development, fitness, and enjoyment of the sport\. Prior to that, he coached extensively in Brazil at Top Tennis, Chácara do Abaeté, and Niterói Racket Club, where he coordinated youth and adult training programs and organized community tournaments\.

Thiago brings a unique blend of technical tennis instruction and physical education training, with a background in physical therapy and multiple certifications from both Tennis Canada and the Brazilian Tennis Federation\. His coaching style is energetic, student\-centered, and rooted in long\-term athlete development principles\.

title: Move UBC Events
content_markdown:
# Welcome to Move UBC

**Move UBC is a university\-wide annual initiative to increase physical activity and reduce the time students, staff, faculty and the UBC community spend sitting**\. Small changes can add up to big impacts—moving more and sitting less can improve both mental and physical health, impact academic and professional success, and contribute to wellbeing in meaningful ways\. This February, make movement apart of your day by getting involved with Move UBC\.

[**Move UBC Events Calendar**](https://wellbeing.ubc.ca/campaigns-initiatives/move-ubc/move-ubc-events-calendar)

#### Explore different ways to get involved with Move UBC during the month of February\! 

---

### Move UBC Recess

#### February 2 \| Free In\-Person Event

To kick off Move UBC Month, **join us for Recess with the Move U Crew at MacInnes on Monday, February 2 from 12:00\-2:00pm\!** Meet us at MacInnes Field for a variety of fun activities\! We will also have arts and crafts, partner booths, and even nostalgic snacks\!

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Move-U-Crew-feature-1200x375-1.jpg)

---

### Yoga Rave

#### February 6 \| Free In\-Person Event

**Yoga Rave is a glow\-in\-the\-dark yoga dance party, free for UBC students\!** Wear your brightest neon clothes and bring your yoga mat \(or borrow one\)\. Designed for fun and all abilities\.

[***Register for the 6:30 – 7:30 PM Session Here***](https://ubc.perfectmind.com/24063/Classes/BookMe4LandingPages/CoursesLandingPage?courseId=c0c64993-45fd-4b51-91d2-960fda44bc40&_gl=1*w7nnnj*_gcl_aw*R0NMLjE3NjQ3MjIxOTguQ2owS0NRaUF1YnJKQmhDYkFSSXNBSElkeEQtcTVTclpKeHlEZjI4cTlrVG0xalNXWUYxRHhmOTJiallncGJUQXRNM0pMejJ0REFVZVN3SWFBcWJyRUFMd193Y0I.*_gcl_au*MTU2MTYwMTA2LjE3NjM0MjYzNTg.*_ga*NjU5OTE1MDAyLjE3NDcxODIzNzA.*_ga_8J87JYF15S*czE3NjYwODk1NjEkbzUyMCRnMSR0MTc2NjA5NTYyNiRqNjAkbDAkaDA.)

[***Register for the 8:00 – 9:00 PM Session Here***](https://ubc.perfectmind.com/24063/Classes/BookMe4LandingPages/CoursesLandingPage?courseId=51a07506-0f75-4f85-bf8a-969a0c027ca9&_gl=1*w7nnnj*_gcl_aw*R0NMLjE3NjQ3MjIxOTguQ2owS0NRaUF1YnJKQmhDYkFSSXNBSElkeEQtcTVTclpKeHlEZjI4cTlrVG0xalNXWUYxRHhmOTJiallncGJUQXRNM0pMejJ0REFVZVN3SWFBcWJyRUFMd193Y0I.*_gcl_au*MTU2MTYwMTA2LjE3NjM0MjYzNTg.*_ga*NjU5OTE1MDAyLjE3NDcxODIzNzA.*_ga_8J87JYF15S*czE3NjYwODk1NjEkbzUyMCRnMSR0MTc2NjA5NTYyNiRqNjAkbDAkaDA.)

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/yoga-rave.jpg)

---

### RAD Try It Night

#### February 9 \| Free In\-Person Event

[Recreation Adapted \(RAD\) Society](https://www.radsociety.ca/aboutrad), is an organization who believes a paralyzing injury doesn’t mean the end of an active, outdoor lifestyle\. Come try out their suite of equipment at Rec North’s indoor track\! This event is intended for people with all abilities\. Register by February 9\!

[***Register***](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0IIGnSqaLitEl94) 

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Rad-Feature-Image_1200x475.jpg)

---

### Move UBC Keynote: The Power of Movement for Resilience with Olympian Clara Hughes 

#### February 24 \| Free In\-Person Event

As part of Move UBC’s 10\-year anniversary, join Olympian and mental health advocate Clara Hughes on Tuesday, February 24, 1:30\-3 pm at the UBC Vancouver Telus Studio Theatre, Chan Centre and a livestreamed UBC Okanagan watch party in the SUO Theatre \(UNC106\)\. Clara will share her experiences as a high\-performance athlete and explore how movement can support resilience, mental health, and overall wellbeing both on campus and beyond\. 

UBC students, faculty, and staff are invited to get their complimentary ticket below\.

[***Get Your Tickets Here\!***](https://tickets.ubc.ca/online/seatSelect.asp?createBO::WSmap=1&BOparam::WSmap::loadBestAvailable::performance_ids=747C4B9C-1742-43E4-900C-CF5124599D50)

### [Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Chan-Centre_Clara-Hughes_1280x940-768x564.jpg)

[**Presenter Information**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/get-moving/move-ubc-events/#presenter-information-19)

This year's Keynote speaker is Clara Hughes\. Clara is a multi\-sport Olympian, one of the few to compete in both the Winter and Summer Olympics\. Hughes earned two bronze medals in the 1996 Summer Olympics and four medals over the course of three Winter Olympics\. Her decorated past has led her to be recognized in Canada's Sport Hall of Fame\. 

Clara's story aligns closely with UBC's commitment to advancing wellbeing through teaching, learning, research, and campus culture\. Her voice spotlights physical activity not only for physical health but as a key contributor to mental wellbeing\. 

---

### Just Dance UBC

#### February 26 \| Free In\-Person Event

In partnership with the Move U Crew and UBC's Heart & Stroke Club, the closing event for Move UBC is putting on Just Dance in the Nest Atrium from noon to 1:00 pm\! No experience needed\. No judgment\. Just hit songs, simple follow\-along moves, and a room full of energy\.

Whether you’re dancing for fun, fitness, or just to shake off the day, Just Dance makes moving your body feel effortless and exciting\. Just Dance turns music into movement and exercise into fun\!

*No registration required, drop by on the day of at noon and hangout\!*

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/ChaChaDance8.jpg)

---

title: Player Performance
content_markdown:
**We are proud the introduce the UBC Baseball Department of Player Performance\!** The Department of Player Performance is a branch of the UBC Baseball organization\. It encompasses all aspects of player development including assessments, training, research, and sport performance recommendations\. We leverage technology, data analysis, and evidence\-based methods to inform our training and to better understand what each athlete is capable of so they can work to reach their full potential\.

[Embedded iframe \(view source\)](https://www.youtube.com/embed/7es8MfLEG_Q)

## **Why did we create it?**

Baseball is changing\. The amount of technology and information being used for player development at the professional, college, and high school levels is more than ever before\. Organizations across North America are implementing new developmental approaches and players throughout all levels are benefiting considerably\. Coaches are able to gain a better understanding of a player’s strengths and weaknesses and it allows them to develop the best plan of action going forward\. As our organization continues to rapidly grow, we found that we needed a way to ensure that all of the players training with us are provided with the right information to grow and progress in the sport of baseball\. Our goal is to educate players and coaches and to provide them with knowledge and resources to enhance the development process\.

## **Who did we create it for?**

We created it for the player that wants more\. Little league to the professional level, every player can benefit from a better understanding of their strengths and weaknesses as well as other aspects of development that are key to baseball performance\.

## **Technology**

[**HitTrax**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/baseball/player-performance/#hittrax-12)

Measures batted ball metrics:

-   **Exit velocity** – is the observed speed the ball leaves the bat \(MPH\)
-   **Launch angle** – is the angle at which the ball leaves the bat\. A positive launch angle means the ball is going up, negative is down, and zero is level to the ground
-   **Distance** – is the distance the ball would travel if hitting on a field
-   **Point of impact** – the point \(x, y, z coordinate\) the ball was struck by the bat in relation to the origin \(back point of plate\)

[**Blast Motion**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/baseball/player-performance/#blast-motion-13)

Measures bat kinematics:

-   **Bat speed** – is the observed speed of the sweet spot of the bat at impact\. The sweet spot of the bat is measured six inches from the tip of the bat\.
-   **Peak Hand speed** – is the observed maximum speed as measured on the handle of the bat \(measured six inches from the knob of the bat\)\. Peak Hand Speed will occur prior to the moment of impact, very close to the commit time in the swing when the wrists unhinge\.
-   **Time to contact** – is the elapsed time between start of downswing and impact\. The start of downswing uses an advanced algorithm to detect when functional forward Bat Speed is initiated and is not triggered by bat waggle early in the swing\.
-   **Attack Angle** – is the angle of the bat’s path, at impact, relative to horizontal\. A positive value indicates swinging up, and a negative value indicates swinging down, where zero is perfectly level\.

[**Rapsodo**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/baseball/player-performance/#rapsodo-14)

Measures pitching metrics:

-   **Pitch velocity** – The speed of the pitch, measure in MPH
-   **Spin rate** – the speed the ball is spinning, measured in RPMs
-   **Spin efficiency** – The degree to which the spin of the ball is playing to the pitches advantage \(e\.g\. greater spin efficiency on a curveball means the spin has more of an influence on what the ball is doing\)
-   **Horizontal & Vertical break** – the amount of break the pitch has, measured in inches\.

[**Performance Testing**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/baseball/player-performance/#performance-testing-15)

Speed/Power/Agility

## **Baseball Assessments**

[**What is the purpose of an assessment?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/baseball/player-performance/#what-is-the-purpose-of-an-asse-16)

-   To gain an in\-depth understanding of a player’s current strengths and weaknesses
-   To inform programming on a more individualized level by using assessment results to tweak the training to the specific needs of the individual
-   To track progress over time

[**Who is it for?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/baseball/player-performance/#who-is-it-for-17)

Little League to Professional Players \(Ages 9\+\)

[**What does an assessment include?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/baseball/player-performance/#what-does-an-assessment-includ-18)

**Baseline Assessment** **– Individual \($262\.49 per player \)**

-   Hittrax \(hitting\)
-   Rapsodo \(pitching\)
-   Hittrax & Blast \(Hitting\) \-or\- Rapsodo \(Pitching\) Reports
-   Additional video component
-   Additional analysis \(practice/drill recommendations\) with coach
-   Comparative analysis

## Private Training Single Session

-   Available for players that are 9\-years\-old or older
-   Pitching, hitting and fielding instruction available
-   **1\-Session \= $150/hour \(tax included\)**

## Private Training Memberships

Player Performance memberships are available for players that are 9\-years\-old or older\.

**4\-Session Membership \= $525 \(tax included\)**

-   Basic Assessment included \(no report\)
-   Must use within 1\-month of purchase
-   No group sessions allowed

**12\-Session Membership \= $1,449 \(tax included\)**

-   Free regular assessment included \(Value \= $250\)
-   Data tracking through Rapsodo and HitTrax
-   Must use within 3\-months of purchase

**24\-Session Membership \= $2,646 \(tax included\)**

-   Free regular assessment included \(Value \= $250\)
-   Data tracking through Rapsodo and HitTrax
-   Must use within 6\-months of purchase
-   One additional follow up assessment

## **Ready to start?**

Complete the Player Performance Intake Form and one of our coaches will get back to you about getting you started on improving your player performance\.

[**Player Performance Intake Form**](https://forms.recreation.ubc.ca/baseball-player-performance-intake-form/)

*For inquires and questions, email our team for more details [baseball\.performance@ubc\.ca](mailto:baseball.performance@ubc.ca)*

title: Baseball Cage Rentals
content_markdown:
# Baseball Cage Rentals

The UBC Baseball Rose Indoor Training Centre \(RITC\) is home to the UBC Thunderbirds Baseball Team and is a state\-of\-the\-art indoor training facility located beside the Tourmaline West Baseball Stadium\. Designed for baseball, with 4 full\-size batting cages and pitching machines, the RITC is the premiere baseball facility in British Columbia\. Visit our [About the UBC Baseball Rose Indoor Training Centre \(RITC\) page](https://sportfacilities.ubc.ca/baseball-tc/) to learn more about cage rentals and the amenities in the facility\. 

### How to Book a Cage Rental

1.  You may book a cage no more than 72 hours in advance \(e\.g\. if you wish to book a court at 4:00PM on Monday, you cannot book prior to 4:00PM on the Friday before\)\. 
2.  All bookings will occur in 1\-hour fixed time slots that start at the beginning of each hour\. 
3.  Persons interested in cage rentals will be required to create a [UBC Recreation account](https://portal.recreation.ubc.ca/) and add at least one credit card to your account, then contact the Baseball Centre at 604\.822\.5770 or [itc\.info@ubc\.ca\.](mailto:itc.info@ubc.ca)  
4.  All cage fees must be paid in full at the time of the booking\. Only credit \(Visa or Mastercard\) or debit payment is accepted at this time\. 
5.  Pitching machines must be requested at the time of booking\. 
6.  Participants will check in with UBC Baseball Centre staff to verify their time slot and sign required waivers\. 
7.  Participants are encouraged to bring their own equipment; however, equipment \(bats, helmet, batting tee\) can be provided upon request\. If equipment is damaged or stole, an additional charge may be applied\.  
8.  Once the sign\-in is complete, participants are required to wait in the lobby until the previous group leaves the cage\. 
9.  After the booking, participants must clean up all balls and leave the cage as they found it\.  
10.  All cage bookings are non\-refundable\. 

**Rentals can be requested by calling 604\-822\-5770 or by emailing [itc\.info@ubc\.ca](mailto:itc.info@ubc.ca) for booking requests\.** 

##### Please Note

-   When signing\-in you will: be assigned a cage, sign a paper waiver/consent form, and have the option to rent helmets or bats at the sign\-in desk\. 
-   Only 1 helmet per individual and only 2 bats per rental group\. 
-   Baseballs will be provided \(or softballs for slo\-pitch rentals\)\. 
-   We recommend that players bring their own batting gloves\. 
-   No metal spikes on shoes permitted inside the facility\. 
-   No food/beverage/gum, other than water\. 
-   Up to two cages can be booked during a 24 hour window\.  
-   A maximum of 4 players can be in a cage at any given time\. 
-   Cage bookings may be moved after confirmation to a different cage number to prevent schedule gaps and as required\. 
-   All cage bookings must be vacated promptly at the end of the booking to allow for the next group to enter\. 
-   Cage bookings cannot be used for private lessons\. Only UBC Baseball coaches are authorized to provide instruction in the facility\. Patrons who appear to be conducting private will be issued a warning or asked to leave without refund\.   

### Cage Rental Prices

Current cage booking prices are listed below\.  

*Prices in effect until March 31, 2026\. Prices do not include GST\.*

| Single Batting Cage/Pitching Area – Prime | $58\.00 | $42\.00 | $52\.00 | $37\.00 |
| Single Batting Cage/Pitching Area – Non\-Prime | $42\.00 | N/A | $37\.50 | N/S |
| Pitching Machines | $25\.00 | $25\.00 | $25\.00 | $25\.00 |

**Prime Hours \(Sep – Mar\)**

-   Mon – Fri: 4:30 pm – 9:00 pm
-   Sat – Sun: 9:00 am – 9:00 pm

**Non\-Prime Hours \(Sep – Mar\)**

-   Mon – Fri: 8:00 am – 4:30 pm

\*Current Hours of Operation can be found on our [Contact Baseball](https://recreation.ubc.ca/baseball/contact/) page\.

\[1\] UBC Students who have setup a login using their CWL are automatically eligible for discounted rates when booking online or through the phone/email\.

title: Locations & Facilities
content_markdown:
# Take a virtual tour of UBC’s sport facilities

Consider this map a guide to the UBC’s sport facilities and the wide variety of programs offered through UBC Recreation\. Highlight and click on a sport facility for a virtual 360° tour as well as highlights and available activities at each location\.

*For best browsing experience, please use a desktop browser\. Mobile and touchscreen devices may not initiate the virtual tours or work as intended\.*

**×**

#### John M\.S\. Lecky UBC Boathouse

[7277 River Road, Richmond](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=UBC+Boathouse+BC)

Located 18km south east of UBC’s Point Grey campus, the UBC Boathouse is a mixed use venue on the shore of the Fraser River supporting rowing/paddling programs\. It also acts as an idyllic backdrop for events and weddings\.

##### Facility Features

-   Boat bays and dock to support rowing and dragon boat activities
-   Change and wash rooms
-   Event hall and patio for weddings, reception, and other hosted events

##### Activities

-   Learn to Row & adult Thunder community rowing team
-   Youth rowing development & Thunder rowing team
-   Event hall and patio for weddings, reception, and other hosted events

**Close**

**×**

#### Thunderbird Stadium

[6288 Stadium Road](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=Thunderbird+Stadium+BC)

Thunderbird Stadium is an open\-air, artificial turf stadium used primarily for soccer, football, and rugby\. The stadium opened on October 7, 1967 and can seat 3,500 in the main grandstand\. By using the surrounding grass embankment the facility can accommodate up to 12,000 spectators\. In 2017, the UBC Homecoming game between the Thunderbirds and the Saskatchewan Huskies had the top football attendance, estimated over 10,000\.

##### Facility Features

-   Fully lit, artificial turf suitable for day/night and all\-weather use
-   Team change and wash rooms
-   Covered seating for 3,500; additional capacity for 5,000 spectators on west embankment

##### Activities

-   Weekly intramural soccer league for UBC students, faculty, and staff
-   Home to UBC Thunderbirds varsity football & soccer games

**Close**

**×**

#### Thunderbird Park

[2700 East Mall](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=Thunderbird+Park+BC)

Thunderbird Park is a sprawling collection of turf and grass fields near the south end of the UBC campus that are host to a variety of teams, student leagues, and community activities\. Including the adjacent Rashpal Dhillon Track & Field Oval, Thunderbird Park provides extensive opportunities for organized recreation as well as less formal activities like walking or pick\-up soccer games during less busy times\.

Between September to April, expect to see Thunderbird Park bustling in the evenings and weekends as it’s not unusual for the intramural soccer and ultimate leagues to be running for students while Thunderbirds varsity teams like field hockey and rugby may also be hosting important matches\.

##### Facility Features

-   Accessible change & wash rooms at the National Soccer Development Centre \(NSDC\)
-   Fully lit, artificial turf fields for day/night and all\-weather use
    -   Ken Woods Field
    -   Warren Field
-   Wright Field – dedicated turf, field hockey field
-   Natural grass fields with rugby uprights
    -   Wolfson East Field
    -   Buck Field
    -   Lord Field
-   Tourmaline West Baseball Stadium and Rashpal Dhillon Track & Field Oval are additional facilities at Thunderbird Park

##### Activities

-   Weekly intramural soccer and Ultimate frisbee leagues for UBC students, faculty, & staff
-   Community leagues including the Thunderbird Adult Soccer League
-   Varsity rugby & field hockey home games

**Close**

**×**

#### Tourmaline West Baseball Stadium

[3085 Wesbrook Mall](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=Tourmaline+West+Baseball+Stadium+BC)

Tourmaline West Stadium is the first artificial turf baseball field in the province of British Columbia\. Completed in 2018, the baseball stadium is home to varsity, junior varsity, and younger community baseball teams\. In 219, the stadium and the UBC Thunderbirds varsity baseball team hosted the International Collegiate Baseball Classic featuring two Japanese universities \(Keio University and University Tokyo\) and NCAA Div I team, Sacramento State University\.

##### Facility Features

-   AstroTurf surface for natural grass feel and all\-weather use
-   4 AstroTurf Bullpens
-   Portable on\-field mounds and fence that allow for field conversions to softball, slo\-pitch or little league
-   Outfield available for flag football, softball, and ultimate frisbee rentals
-   Dimensions: RF – 98\.1 \(322 feet\); CF – 113\.1m \(371 feet\); LF – 98\.1m \(322 feet\)

##### Activities

-   Watch the UBC Thunderbirds varsity baseball team play in the spring

**Close**

**×**

#### UBC Baseball Rose Indoor Training Centre

[3085 Wesbrook Mall](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=UBC+Baseball+Rose+Indoor+Training+Centre+BC)

The UBC Baseball Rose Indoor Training Centre \(RITC\) is home to the UBC Thunderbirds Baseball Team and is a state\-of\-the\-art indoor training facility located beside the Tourmaline West Baseball Stadium\. It is heated allowing a comfortable training environment year round\. Designed for baseball, with 4 full\-size batting cages and pitching machines, the RITC is the premiere baseball facility in British Columbia\. The facility also has the ability to convert and be used for multi\-sport training\.

##### Facility Features

-   4 full\-size batting cages \(Astroturf\) with dividers
-   1 designated pitching area \(Astroturf\) with 2 pitching mounds and training equipment
-   4 pitching machines
-   3 HitTrax data capture and simulation systems
-   UBC Baseball team store

##### Activities

-   Batting cage rentals
-   Youth & BC PBL baseball programs
-   Player performance coaching supported by state\-of\-the\-art technology

**Close**

**×**

#### Gerald McGavin UBC Rugby Centre

[2765 Wesbrook Mall](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=Gerald+McGavin+UBC+Rugby+Centre+BC)

Located in the heart of UBC’s athletic venues and pristine playing fields, the Gerald McGavin Rugby Centre offers an expansive view of Thunderbird Park’s grass fields\. Its raised terrace and exterior, stadium style seating makes for a great viewing location of UBC Thunderbirds varsity rugby games or to simply enjoy the lush, green landscape\.

##### Facility Features

-   100\-person interior lounge
-   Covered terrace
-   Exterior stadium seating for up to 100 guests
-   Team change rooms & offices for UBC Thunderbirds varsity rugby

**Close**

**×**

#### UBC Tennis Centre

[6160 Thunderbird Boulevard](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=UBC+Tennis+Centre+BC)

The UBC Tennis Centre is one of Vancouver’s only public, indoor tennis facilities\. The facility includes 12 indoor courts across two buildings as well as one outdoor court\. The UBC Tennis Centre is set up to provide great, year round access to tennis whether you’re looking for great coaching through the lessons and drill programs, booking a court rental, or playing in a tennis Grand Slam mixer event\.

##### Facility Features

-   8 indoor courts at the UBC Tennis Centre
-   4 indoor courts at the UBC Tennis Bubble
-   1 outdoor court
-   Accessible wash & change room facilities
-   Tennis racquet re\-stringing
-   Day\-use lockers

##### Activities

-   Tennis court rentals, including discounted rates for UBC Students
-   Coached lessons – skills, drills, and clinics – for adults, youth, and students
-   Performance tennis programs for youth development and adults
-   Weekly leagues, Grand Slam mixer events for a blend of social and competition

**Close**

**×**

#### Doug Mitchell Thunderbird Sports Centre

[6066 Thunderbird Boulevard](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=Doug+Mitchell+Thunderbird+Sports+Centre+BC)

Thunderbird Arena was host venue for the 2010 Olympic and Paralympic Games and can hold up to 7,000 people for special events like the UBC Winter Classic hockey game or concerts\. This venue is the home of UBC Thunderbirds ice hockey teams and is also accessible for sledge hockey\. The Father David Bauer Arena and the Protrans Arena are primarily used for hockey related programs hockey and skating lessons, public skating sessions, and two hockey leagues\.

The facility also features pro shop that carries some hockey and skating equipment as well as providing services such as skate rentals and skate sharpening\.

##### Facility Features

There are three sheets of ice at the Doug Mitchell Thunderbird Sports Centre:

-   Thunderbird Arena
-   Father David Bauer Arena
-   Protrans Arena

##### Activities

-   Free public skating for UBC Students
-   Learn to skate programs for youth and adults
-   Drop\-in sessions for stick & puck, hockey, skating, and figure skating

**Close**

**×**

#### War Memorial Gym

[6081 University Boulevard](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=War+Memorial+Gym+BC)

The UBC War Memorial Gymnasium is located in the centre of the University of British Columbia Point Grey campus, adjacent to the Nest \(the Student Union Building\), the Robert H\. Lee Alumni Centre, the Student Recreation Centre and the UBC Aquatic Centre\. The building is

##### Facility Features

-   Gymnasium can hold up to 4 volleyball courts and features a main basketball court
-   Full service dressing rooms and showers

##### Activities

-   Home of the UBC Thunderbirds varsity basketball & volleyball teams – check out home games on Friday & Saturday evenings 

**Close**

**×**

#### UBC Aquatic Centre

[6080 Student Union Boulevard](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=UBC+Aquatic+Centre+BC)

The UBC Aquatic Centre is a state\-of\-the\-art facility that serves athletic training, competition, and neighbourhood leisure needs\. The facility’s natatorium can accommodate nearly 1,000 bathers, and the viewing area in the mezzanine can host up to 460 spectators\.

##### Facility Features

-   25 metre recreational pool with 1m and 3m diving boards and accessible ramp
-   50 metre competition pool with Omega Swiss Timing System
-   Leisure pool and lazy river with accessible ramp
-   34\-person family friendly hot tub with accessibility lift
-   Steam room and sauna
-   Men’s, women’s, and universal change rooms
-   Term locker rentals and day lockers
-   Accessible entrances with power\-operated doors
-   Accessible washrooms, change rooms, ramps and lifts
-   Braille signage

##### Activities

-   Free leisure, length, and student\-specific swims for UBC Students
-   Swim lessons, first\-aid, aquatic safety & certification courses
-   Artistic Swimming Thunderbirds Sport Club

**Close**

**×**

#### Student Recreation Centre

[6000 Student Union Boulevard](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=UBC+Student+Recreation+Centre+BC)

Home of UBC Recreation, the UBC Student Recreation Centre offers over 17,000 sq ft with a triple court gymnasium for volleyball, basketball, badminton, and indoor soccer \(futsal\)\.

Additionally, the facility features a 2,300 sq ft dance studio with stretching bars and a 1,600 sq ft martial arts dojo with matted floor\.

##### Facility Features

-   Triple court gymnasium

### Welcome to the Indigenous Wellbeing Series

**The Indigenous Wellbeing Series is live\!** This monthly event series for Indigenous students, staff, and faculty will offer holistic and culturally relevant ways to make time for wellness\. Student wellness is key to student success in meeting personal, career, and academic goals\. The Indigenous Wellbeing Series is organized by UBC Rec and the Wellness Centre\. 

#### Previous Events

[**All My Relations Meditation** **\- November 16**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/get-moving/indigenous-wellbeing-series/#all-my-relations-meditation-no-8)

**Tuesday, Nov 16th at 12pm – All My Relations Meditation** \(30 min\.\) 

A guided mindfulness practice and prayer meditation to align our breath, mind, body, and spirit\.

Participants must pre\-register below to receive the zoom link\. The class will also be streamed in the Dojo of the [Student Recreation Centre](https://sportfacilities.ubc.ca/src/)\. If you are coming to watch the stream in person, please remember your BC Vaccine Card and government\-issued ID\!

A slow, gentle vinyasa yoga practice and moving meditation to support balance and creativity\. 

Participants must pre\-register below to receive the zoom link\. The class will also be streamed in the Dojo of the [Student Recreation Centre](https://sportfacilities.ubc.ca/src/)\. If you are coming to watch the stream in person, please remember your BC Vaccine Card and government\-issued ID\! 

[**Register for the Indigenous Wellbeing Series: Flowing with Creation Yoga**](https://ubc.zoom.us/meeting/register/u5Apde-oqzIsHdKyrJAgbi-Wj0aOBZAGrl_R)

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/image005-241x300.jpg)

[**Kick\-Off Wellbeing Walk \- September 24**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/get-moving/indigenous-wellbeing-series/#kick-off-wellbeing-walk-septem-10)

Join us for the first event of this series \- the Kick\-Off Wellbeing Walking Tour\! This tour will be led by the Indigenous Student Ambassadors and is a chance to explore various parts of the beautiful campus with a hot drink in hand\!

The event will be held on **September 24th from 4:00pm to 5:30pm**\. The meeting place will be a coffee shop on campus so that folks can get a warm beverage prior to the walk\. More information about the meeting place to come soon\.

## Learn About the Project

The Recreation Centre North facility will be built on the large plaza space situated immediately north of the UBC Life Building \(formerly the Student Union Building\) and at the western end of Student Union Boulevard\. Located at the heart of UBC’s Vancouver campus, the building will include an outdoor walkway corridor at ground level to allow foot traffic to readily flow through the area\.

The building is designed by SHAPE Architecture and features an indoor floor area of 101,000 square feet spread over four levels, including three gymnasium courts; an indoor run, roll, walk track; cardio and weightlifting areas; multipurpose rooms; universal and gender\-specific change areas; and administrative offices\. The Recreation Centre North will also be constructed to a LEED Gold green building standard and is Rick Hansen Foundation Certified\.

Construction began in 2022 and was completed in summer 2025\. The projet cost is $67\.5 million including contributions from UBC, Alma Mater Society \(AMS\) student fees, and donors\.

*Thank you to supporters of the Activate UBC campaign that is helping to build Recreation Centre North\.*

This new activity and fitness centre will provide the UBC community a space to connect and get moving\. The new building will house state\-of\-the\-art exercise opportunities including three full gymnasiums courts, strength and cardio equipment, functional training and multipurpose spaces, running track and more\. This facility will support our UBC student’s fitness and wellbeing goals and will provide them a space to prioritize their mental and physical health while they are pursuing their academic achievements\. title: Moves on MacInnes
content_markdown:
### Moves on MacInnes *provides free sports and activity equipment to the UBC community for use on MacInnes Field\. [As part of an investment from the University of British Columbia towards increasing access to student recreation](https://recreation.ubc.ca/2021/10/20/new-funding-creates-more-recreation-opportunities-for-ubc-students/), the* Moves on MacInnes *program is designed to encourage informal activities and social opportunities at the heart of UBC’s Vancouver campus\.*

## Available Equipment

-   Ultimate discs
-   Jump ropes & fitness equipment
-   Spikeball sets
-   Soccer balls
-   Rugby Balls

## How to Borrow Equipment

To borrow any of the available equipment, visit the UBC Student Recreation Centre’s front desk\. You will need to provide a government photo ID or UBC Card as a deposit to sign out the equipment\. When you’re done using the equipment, return it to the SRC and you will receive back your ID\. Equipment must be returned on the same day it is borrowed, and must be returned prior to the SRC closing\.

## Late Returns & Broken Equipment

Any and all equipment not returned prior to the SRC’s closing time on the original date of rental will be subject to a $20\.00 per day late fee\. Equipment returned in broken or not in good working condition will be subject to broken equipment fees:

| Equipment | Late Fee \(per day\) | Broken Equipment Fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spikeball set | $20\.00 | $80\.00 |
| Football | $20\.00 | $25\.00 |
| Frisbee | $20\.00 | $25\.00 |
| Soccer ball | $20\.00 | $25\.00 |
| Rugby ball | $20\.00 | $25\.00 |

## Suggest New Activities & Equipment

Feel like we’re missing something? Share your feedback with [rec\.operations@ubc\.ca](mailto:rec.operations@ubc.ca) to suggest equipment, activities, or improvements for the *Moves on MacInnes* program\.

title: UBC-V Sports Day
content_markdown:
## **About the Event** 

### **What is UBC Faculty & Staff Sports Day?** 

This event is designed for faculty and staff members of UBC to have fun and get moving with their colleagues\. Aligned with the UBC People and Places Plan as well as the UBC Wellbeing Strategic Framework, this event seeks to foster wellbeing and thriving communities through physical activity and social connection\. This event is perfect for colleagues looking for an afternoon of activities that facilitate teamwork, communication, and getting to know one another\.  

Join us with a team of 4\-6 for an afternoon of fun on the UBC Point Grey Campus on the traditional, ancestral and unceded territory of the Musqueam people\. Teams will participate in various games and activities followed by an “apres” social time with snacks and beverages\. 

### **Event Details** 

The event is divided into two time slots\. Each time slot will offer an hour and a half for activities followed by a 30 min\. “apres” option\. Teams can spend up to the full hour and a half participating in activities, or head to the “apres” area to enjoy snacks and beverages\.  

### **How Can I Participate?** 

Faculty and staff members can register as an individual or a team\. If you register as an individual, you will be placed with others to make a team of 4\-6 members\.  

You can also register as a team of 4\-6 team members\. A designated Team Captain will register on behalf of the team\. The Team Captain will be able to add their team members to their roster once registered\. 

### **What if I am not sporty?** 

Faculty and staff sports day is for everyone\! A wide range of activities will be offered to accommodate varying levels of experience, fitness and ability\.  Every activity will have a physical activity level rating\. Teams will be able to choose which activities they want to participate in as well as how many\. 

---

## **Event Registration**

**In\-Person – Team & Individual Registration** 

In\-person activities will be taking place on the UBC Point Grey Campus on the traditional, ancestral and unceded territory of the Musqueam people\. The event will be separated into two time slots \(12:00pm and 2:00pm starts\) with up to 1\.5 hours of activity time followed by a 30 minute social period for team to connect over free snacks and beverages\.   

Teams of 4\-6 people or individuals can sign\-up to participate for the in\-person event\. Individuals signing up for the in\-person event will be placed on teams with other registered individuals\. **Please note that all parties registering for the in\-person will also be signed\-up to receive information about the virtual activities but are not required to complete them\.** 

Teams can register as Just for Fun or Competitive\.   

-   **Just for Fun Teams Objective**: Have fun\!  
-   **Competitive Teams Objective:** Complete as many activities as possible within the 1\.5\-hour timeslot\. Teams must hand in their passport at the finish line before 1:30pm/3:30pm \(respective of timeslots\) to be eligible to win\.   

---

## In\-Person Event Schedule 

The in\-person events on Friday, May 1, 2026 are broken into two time slots: 

### Group \#1 – 12:00 – 1:30 PM

**11:00 AM** – Pre\-race check\-in available

**12:00\-1:30 PM** – Activity time

**1:30\-2:00 PM** – Social Time \(with snacks & beverages\)

### Group \#2 – 2:00 – 3:30 PM

**1:30 PM** – Pre\-race check\-in available

**2:00\-3:30 PM** – Activity Time

**3:30 – 4:00 PM** – Social Time \(with snacks & beverages\)

### **Awards Ceremonies** 

Winners will be awarded for each timeslot\. A small awards ceremony will be held during the respective social times to announce the sports day winners and other fun awards and prizes\!   

[**Register for Sports Day at UBC\-V**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sportsday/register/)

title: Intramural Uniform Orders
content_markdown:
UBC Recreation Intramurals provides team uniform orders as an inexpensive way to kit your team in t\-shirts or hockey jerseys that meet the requirements for its league sports programs\. All uniforms feature player numbers on the back and the choice of a custom or UBC Thunderbirds logo on the front\.

The ordering process is comprised of a few key steps:

-   [Uniform Design](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/#design)
-   [Online Payment & Ordering](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/#order)
-   [Confirm Uniform Details](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/#confirm)
-   [Pick\-up of Uniforms](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/#pick-up)

## Design Your Team’s Uniform

Before ordering your team’s uniforms, please take some time to review the available options and complete any design work required\. This will ensure that your order is processed without delay and delivered quickly\.

### Uniform Logo

On the front of each set of team uniforms, you can choose from one of three options:

-   [Custom logo](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/#custom-logo) – single colour print up to 8″ x 10″
-   Thunderbirds logo – single colour print, 8″ x 10″ on centre of chest
-   No logo

### Uniform Colour

Select the uniform colour:

[https://recreation\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/09/2022\-league\-uniform\-colours\.png](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2022-league-uniform-colours.png)[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2022-league-uniform-colours.png)

### Uniform Type

Select the uniform type:

-   Hockey jersey
-   Cotton t\-shirt

> *\*\* Please note: Intramurals reserves the right to change or disallow any team name, logo, or uniform that is in poor taste or offensive under the UBC Intramurals policy on Team Names\.* *This policy is in accordance with the UBC Policy on Discrimination and Harassment and the commitment to a safe & equitable recreation experience\.\*\**

## Submit & Pay for Team Uniforms Online

Once you know the details of your team’s uniforms, please submit an online order and payment to begin the process for team uniforms\. After clicking on the appropriate link below, use the walkthrough to ensure you submit your order correctly\.

[**T\-Shirt Uniforms**](https://ubc.perfectmind.com/24063/Classes/BookMe4LandingPages/CoursesLandingPage?courseId=3d60e18d-6fc7-447b-bd37-ea89c92a2d23)

[**Hockey Jersey Uniforms**](https://ubc.perfectmind.com/24063/Classes/BookMe4LandingPages/CoursesLandingPage?courseId=66c41544-b9c7-4818-bc01-c9189149f301)

### Select “Book” on the event page and then ensure you book yourself as a registrant in this course\.

*If you are not already logged into your UBC Recreation login, you will be prompted to login with your CWL after you press the “Book” button on the first screen\. **Please also ensure that personal information including email address and phone number are accurately updated as these will be used to contact you when your order is ready\.***

[https://recreation\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/09/2022\-league\-uniform\-1\.png](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2022-league-uniform-1.png)[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2022-league-uniform-1.png)

[https://recreation\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/09/2022\-league\-uniform\-2\.png](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2022-league-uniform-2.png)[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2022-league-uniform-2.png)

### Select the correct quantity of uniforms for your order

*Uniform sizing will be collected separately after the online payment is completed\.*

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2022-league-uniform-3-940x464.png)

### Submit online payment for team uniforms

*Verify that your shopping cart contains the correct number of uniforms, enter your payment details, and place your order\.*

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2022-league-uniform-4-940x464.png)

## Confirm Order Details

Within 2 business days of placing your order you will receive an email program that will include a link to a questionnaire to confirm the details of your team’s uniforms\. The responses you provide will help put the finishing touches on your order\.

Ensure that you have the following information before completing the questionnaire:

-   League uniform colour
-   Sizing and associated player number for each uniform \(e\.g\. 3 larges with numbers 22, 23, and 16\)
-   [Artwork file in \.eps format for custom logos – must be single colour and single layer](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/#custom-logo)
-   CO\# from your UBC Recreation Login – this information is also available on the receipt from your online order

[https://recreation\.ubc\.ca/intramurals/%%tb\-image\-url%%](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/%%tb-image-url%%)[%%tb\-image\-alt\-text%%](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/2022-league-uniform-5.png)

Find your CO\# within the details of your UBC Recreation profile\.

Uniforms are often delayed by incomplete information, incorrect file uploads or adjustments needed due inappropriate design or team names\.

*If you do not receive an email receipt or have other questions, please contact [intramurals\.info@ubc\.ca](mailto:intramurals.info@ubc.ca)\.*

## Uniform Pick\-up

All team uniforms are ordered and shipped together to minimize costs associated with production and shipping – these savings are passed along to you\! **While team uniforms are scheduled to arrive by October 14, please wait until you are contacted directly to confirm pick\-up before claiming your order\.**

##### Custom Logo Requirements

**  
×  
**

-   Maximum size of 8″ x 10″
-   Only single colour designs are permitted
    -   Bright colour logos show up best on dark coloured uniforms
    -   Dark colour logos show up best on light coloured uniforms
-   All logo artwork must be submitted in \(\.EPS\) file format \(Encapsulated PostScript\)
-   File must be in black and white and created in a 1:1 scale of the final artwork

title: Thrive
content_markdown:
### **Come move with us as we enter Thrive month\!** 

Each year, UBC dedicates the month of November as a time when we come together as a community to learn and explore ways to support our mental health\. To celebrate Thrive Month, UBC Recreation and Thrive have collaborated to present fun NEW activities open to everyone, with no prior experience needed\. Stay tuned for what programs we will offer this year\!

For the entire month of November, there will be a variety of in\-person and virtual events to encourage the UBC community to prioritize mental health\. For more information about Thrive and other events going on, please see the [Thrive website](https://wellbeing.ubc.ca/wellbeing-campaigns-and-initiatives/thrive)\.

### **Prizes and Giveaways**

Need another reason to get moving? Check out the list below to see what you could win by coming to the event\!

-   Garmin Forerunner 55
-   Spa Gift Basket
-   Lululemon Yoga Mat x2
-   Fitbit
-   Fitness Membership for Term 2 \(UBC Student Only\)
-   Storm the Wall Team Registration \(UBC Student Only\)

### **Instructor Bio: Nyla Bedard**

Nyla Bedard \(Tahltan, Kaska, French, Scottish\) is a multifaceted performing artist currently residing in North Vancouver\. She’s a new mom, a powwow dancer and workshop facilitator\. Drawing on her experience as someone of mixed heritage, her goal is to blend the past, present and create new works for the future\.

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Nyla-Bedard.jpg)

Join us for an indigenous dance class that introduces the different powwow dance styles with focus on traditional, jingle dress and fancy shawl movements\. Come out, get moving and celebrate Indigenous culture through dance\!

title: Thunderbird Takes Flight
content_markdown:
*Strengthening UBC’s relationship with the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm \(Musqueam\) band on whose ancestral lands its Point Grey campus is situated on has been a major commitment in recent years\. In late 2021, UBC’s Athletics and Recreation department initiated a project in partnership with Musqueam to develop an art piece that reflected the Musqueam story of UBC’s sports nickname, the Thunderbirds\.*

*The more than year long process started with over a dozen concepts submitted by Musqueam artists\. A joint group representing Musqueam and UBC pored over the submissions and selected Deanna\-Marie Point’s design because of its strong representation of the characteristics of Musqueam art and dynamic presentation of the Thunderbird\.*

## *Thunderbird Takes Flight*

The thunderbird was created by Mother Earth and Father Sky to communicate their love for each other\. It was the messenger between the two and showed the love and life on earth\. Father Sky controls the weather and the four seasons\. Without the seasons, we could not survive\. If someone saw thunder and lightning in the sky, it meant that Mother Earth was sending a message to Father Sky\. And if they were lucky enough to spot the thunderbird, it brought wealth and good fortune\.

Deanna\-Marie’s version of the Thunderbird represents a significant milestone in the relationship between UBC and the Musqueam people, on whose land UBC’s Vancouver campus is situated\.

For decades, UBC has been associated with the Thunderbirds nickname and has used it with permission from the Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw people since a ceremonial gifting in 1948\. This gifting included the dedication of the Victory Through Honour pole, which features a figure of a Thunderbird at the top\. Based on Kwikwasut’inuxw story of the five tests of Tsikumayi and carved by Ellen Neel, the pole was raised in a public ceremony with permission of the Musqueam people\.

Despite this history, the Thunderbirds story at UBC lacked the same representation and storytelling from the Musqueam people\. Deanna’s artwork marks the first official Musqueam representation of the Thunderbird at UBC\. 

Deanna’s art is being showcased at Storm the Wall, a popular event amongst UBC students that includes scaling a large, 12\-foot high wall where the artwork is featured\. Its use at Storm the Wall is the first stage in a number of new ways that the UBC will be featuring Deanna’s artwork as part of its storytelling about the Thunderbird\.

[Embedded iframe \(view source\)](https://www.youtube.com/embed/a1lLB6rJGC0)

## About the Artist

Deanna\-Marie Point is an emerging xʷməθkʷəy̓əm \(Musqueam\) artist with experience in 2D design, jewelry carving and other visual mediums\. She comes from a family of artists – her mother is a master weaver trained in Musqueam weaving and design, and her father is a carver\. Deanna was raised with cultural and ancestral teachings, which deeply inform her artistic practices\. At a young age, Deanna developed a passion for visual art and would sit with her father and his teachers to learn about traditional Coast Salish art and its history\. Her work has been featured on local TELUS fleet vehicles, indoor and outdoor murals, and the Pride crosswalk installed in Musqueam in 2022\.
