## About the Team

The UBC Thunderbirds Alpine Ski Team is a competitive ski team that competes throughout North America in the United States Collegiate Ski Association \(USCSA\) circuit\. We compete in team\-scored Slalom and Giant Slalom races\. Our season includes two\-day Conference Races within the Northwest Collegiate Ski Conference \(NWCSC\), Regional Championships, and the ultimate goal of returning to the National Championships each year in March\.

The UBC Alpine Ski Team comprises NorAm/FIS/USSA/International athletes, as well as athletes with limited racing experience who aim to enhance their skills\. Training begins in September with dry land, transitioning to weekly on\-snow training at Grouse Mountain\.

Want to learn more? Email our team at [alpineski\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:alpineski.sc@ubc.ca)

A big thanks to our sponsors and UBC alumni whose continued support makes UBC Alpine’s success possible\!

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/alpine-skiing/#how-to-join-370)

UBC Alpine is one of the best university ski teams in Canada, as well as the only Canadian ski team in the USCSA circuit\. We strive to provide our passionate members with the opportunity to continue their racing careers throughout university\. As a member of the team, you will get the opportunity to travel to the United States for conference, regional, and national competitions\. If you want to improve your fitness and develop your skiing, all while building friendships with like\-minded individuals, the UBC Alpine Ski Sport Club is the place for you\!

**Eligibility Requirements:** 

-   Preferred Racing Experience – FIS/NCAA/USSA/NorAM/Club Teams/School Teams
-   Commitment to Fall Dry Land Training: 2x per Week
-   Commitment to Winter On\-Snow Training: 1x per week
-   Commitment to Pre\-Season Camp and Training Weekends
-   Commitment to 2 of 4 Conference Qualifier Races, Regional Championships, and National Championship
-   Commitment to helping at Team Fundraisers

Don’t meet the requirements but still want to join? Email [alpineski\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:alpineski.sc@ubc.ca)

**Try Outs:** 

Tryout location and time TBD\. For more information regarding tryouts, come visit us and your future teammates at UBC’s Imagine Day on Tuesday, September 2, 2025\.

Unable to make it to Imagine Day? Email [alpineski\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:alpineski.sc@ubc.ca)

**Team Fees:**

All of the following fees are approximate and should not be considered as the ultimate amount to be paid\. All values are in Canadian Dollars\. Official fees will be made available to all rostered athletes in advance of the due date and will be communicated through official team channels\.

-   $315 Base Team Fee \(Racing and Training\) Includes:
    -   Team Shirt, Dryland, Team Building Events, Alumni Events, USCSA Registration Fees, Racing Insurance, and Season Training Pass to Grouse Mountain\.
-   $165 Base Team Fee \(Training Only\) Includes:
    -   Team Shirt, Dryland, Team Building Events, Alumni Events, USCSA Registration Fees, and Season Training Pass to Grouse Mountain\.
-   Apparel Fees \(Optional\):
    -   $300 Waterproof Team Jackets
    -   $150 Team Warmup and Practice Gear
    -   More Apparel TBD
-   $350 Single Qualifier Race Fee Includes:
    -   2\-3 Days Worth of Accommodation, Race Fees, Gas, Rental Cars, and Lift Tickets\.
-   $650 Regional Championship Fee Includes:
    -   5\-7 Days Worth of Accommodation, Race Fees, Gas, Rental Cars, and Lift Tickets
-   $500 National Championship Fee Includes:
    -   5\-7 Days Worth of Accommodation, Race Fees, Flights, Luggage Fees, Gas, Rental Cars, and Lift Tickets\.

Approximate single athlete cost for a complete season is $2165 CAD\. This assumes paying for the Base Team Fee \(Racing and Training\), two Qualifier Races, the Regional Championships, and the National Championships\.

Worried about costs? Want to find out more about how we are aiming to lower team fees? Email  
[alpineski\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:alpineski.sc@ubc.ca)

**Practice Schedule:**

Fall Training Stating Mid September:

-   Weekly ARC/Rec North Gym Sessions – Location and Time TBD\.
-   Weekly Field Dryland Sessions – Location and Time TBD\.

Winter Training Starting December:

-   Weekly On\-Hill Training – Grouse Mountain, Time TBD\.

All athletes must attend a **minimum of 75%** of training sessions\.

Worried about attendance and availability? Email [alpineski\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:alpineski.sc@ubc.ca)

**Competition Schedule:** 

Check out [http://www\.uscsanw\.org/](http://www.uscsanw.org/) for more information about the conference and for updates on team and individual standings throughout the season\. Information about our Conference Races, Regional Championships, and National Championships will be communicated through official team channels once it becomes available\.

Generally:

-   Qualifier races occur on weekends from January to early February\. We leave UBC Friday morning and return Sunday night\.
-   Regional Championships occur in mid/late February\.
-   National Championships occur in early/mid\-March\.

[History](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/alpine-skiing/#history-373)

It all began in 1920 with the creation of the Varsity Outdoor Club \(VOC\)\. This club was involved in many outdoor activities, including skiing, and was student run\. By 1928, it was among the most popular clubs on campus\.  
﻿  
[1934 UBC Inter Collegiate Ski Team](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/1934-inter_collegiate-ski-team.jpg)

*1934 UBC Inter Collegiate Ski Team*

In the Spring of 1930, the first alpine competition was introduced, an intramural event that included both a downhill and a cross\-country skiing component\.

Then late in the 1930’s, the UBC Ski Team separated from the VOC and began racing in the Northwest against teams such as the University of Washington\.

[1955 UBC Men's Ski Team](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/UBC-Mens-ski-team-1955.jpg)

*1955 UBC Men’s Ski Team*

By the 1950’s, UBC had become a popular and competitive team\. Al Fisher joined as a volunteer coach in 1956 and was later inducted into the UBC Athletics Hall of Fame \(2003\)\. Fisher combined a passion for fitness and skiing to get the most out of the athletes and, over the years, led some of the University’s most successful ski teams\.

Since the 1950’s, strong Alumni support and a desire to keep a collegiate team in Canada has kept the Skibirds going\.

Until 2015, the UBC Alpine Ski Team was a Varsity Team at UBC, competing in the USCSA circuit\. Since then, the team has restructured into a UBC Thunderbirds Sport Club and remains competitive in the USCSA\. In the 2015\-16 season, the team placed top 3 at the Regional Championships and had one of the strongest UBC showings at Nationals in Lake Placid, New York\. More recently, the team has returned from the pandemic in form, consistently placing top 3 in qualifier races and qualifying for the 2022/2023 USCSA National Championships in Mammoth Lakes, California, the 2023/2024 USCSA National Championships in Lake Placid, New York, and the 2024/2025 USCSA National Championships in Mt\. Bachelor, Oregon\.

## About the Team

UBC Thunderbirds Lacrosse Sport Club was established in 2013 as a student\-run club program that competes against both collegiate and club teams across Western Canada and Northwestern United States\. Since 2013 the UBC Lacrosse team has successfully competed against 5 Canadian university teams in BC and Alberta, defeating 4 of them, and for the\. Starting in 2017 the club travelled to Oregon and Washington to compete against American university club teams\. In 2019 UBC Lacrosse competed in the Canada West Field Lacrosse League, as well as played against Simon Fraser University as part of our commitment to grow collegiate lacrosse in Canada\. This year our goal is to have a successful season in the Canada West Field Lacrosse League and further grow our intercollegiate competition north and south of the border\. For more information visit recreation\.ubc\.ca/sport\-clubs/lacrosse and connect with UBC Lacrosse on [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/pages/Thunderbird-Lacrosse/147911165268163?fref=ts), Instagram \([@ubclax](https://www.instagram.com/ubclax/?hl=en)\), and Twitter \([@ubclax](https://twitter.com/UBCLax)\)\.

For recruitment, donations, sponsorships, or any other inquiries please email us at [lacrosse\.sc@ubc\.ca\.](mailto:lacrosse.sc@ubc.ca)

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/lacrosse/#how-to-join-349)

Anyone interested to compete with UBC Lacrosse should contact us through the [team email](mailto:lacrosse.sc@ubc.ca) or Instagram, [@ubclax](https://www.instagram.com/ubclax/?hl=en)\. More information and arrangements can also be made then\.

The UBC Lacrosse Sport Club’s season runs from September to April\. This year the team will continue to compete in the [Canada West Field Lacrosse League](https://www.cwfll.ca/) throughout the year\. As well, our team is hoping to play in a few select exhibition games against American opponents in the fall, and Canadian opponents in spring\. Joining the team allows you to compete on a weekly basis throughout the academic year and help shape the intercollegiate field lacrosse landscape in western Canada\.

**Try Outs:**

Try\-outs will take place in early September\.

Contact us on our Facebook, Twitter page, or email us at lacrosse\.sc@ubc\.ca to inquire about joining the team\.

**Eligibility Requirements:**

Off Field:

-   UBC requires each player to be registered in 9 credits per term or registered in a UBC affiliated co\-op term\. \(A player can be registered in fewer than 9 credits if they have fulfilled all their academic requirements and are expecting to graduate in that term\.\)
-   Each player must maintain a minimum academic average of 60%\.

On Field:

-   Committed, Encouraging, and always giving their best effort

**Team Fees:**

Team fees will cover team expenses including travel cost, league fees, competition and practice apparel, team insurance and field time\. Additionally, team members will be expected to contribute to meet fundraising goals throughout the season\. Fees cover expected TSC costs, practice uniforms, travel, league fees for games, practice times and practice equipment\. As a club, we do not want money to be a barrier, with proper arrangements, finance plans can be made\.

The team offers varying payment options to accommodate different player’s current financial situation\. Email [lacrosse\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:lacrosse.sc@ubc.ca) for the total breakdown of team fees\.

**Practice Schedule:**

The team practices twice a week on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 9 pm \-11 pm at Warren Field for the winter semester and half of Spring semester, transitioning to Thunderbird Stadium for the last two months of the season\. The team also has a Sunday night lift at the [Bird Coop gym](https://www.google.com/maps/place/BirdCoop+Fitness+Centre/@49.2683905,-123.2511536,17z/data=!3m2!4b1!5s0x548672b76e74acfb:0xfcd08a4a4b215d88!4m5!3m4!1s0x548673f554600589:0xd0873bbbd795289c!8m2!3d49.268387!4d-123.2489649) reserved for all Sport Club Athletes\.

**Competition Schedule:**

The 2022\-2023 competition schedule will be updated soon and can be found on our homepage under “Schedule\.”

Games typically occur on a weekly basis throughout the academic year\. Below is a sample schedule for 2019\-2020\.

-   Fall Intercollegiate competitions \(SFU, Washington state, Oregon\) September – November 2019
-   CWFLL Fall 2019 September  – Nov
-   CWFLL Spring 2020 February – April
-   CWFLL Provincials April 10\-12, 2020

\*Schedule is subject to change, announcements will be on the Instagram \([@ubclax](https://www.instagram.com/ubclax/?hl=en)\) and athletes will be notified\.

[Schedule](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/lacrosse/#schedule-350)

[Results](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/lacrosse/#results-351)

2020/2021: Due to COVID\-19, we were unable to participate in any games or practices\. The Thunderbirds look forward to compete in the CWFLL and against collegiate teams next year\.

2019/2020: Due to COVID\-19, this years season was cut short and we were unable to participate in BC Provincials, however that did not stop us from continuing on our expectations of being successful\. Our program finished mid\-table in 4th place in final CWFLL standings with a 7\-6\-0 record\. In our only competition against SFU and MCLA competition we finished with an 0\-1 record\.

2018/2019: Thunderbirds finished CWFLL regular season with a 9\-7\-1 record\. And in Provincials, the Thunderbirds went 3\-2, finishing in 3rd place in Tier 1\. In 2 PNCLL exhibition games \(vs\. Simon Fraser University\) the Thunderbirds went 1\-1\. The 3rd place finish in provincials was our teams best ever finish and we expect to only grow and maintain our position atop the CWFLL in the coming season\.

2017/2018: In a fall ball tournament taking place in Bend, Oregon against MCLA teams, the Thunderbirds went 4\-0\. Opponents included Montana State University, University of Portland, Central Washington University and Oregon State\. In PNCLL exhibition games, the Thunderbirds defeated Western Washington University, and lost 2 games against Simon Fraser University\. Thunderbirds finished CWFLL regular season play with a 5\-2\-1 record, finished CWFLL Provincials with a 1\-2\-2 record and did not place\.

2016/2017: In a fall ball tournament located at the University of Alberta, the Thunderbirds finished 3\-1 with wins against the University of Alberta and the University of Lethbridge; as well as a win and a lost against the University of Calgary\. In PNCLL exhibition play, the Thunderbirds went 0\-2, dropping both games to Simon Fraser University\. In CWFLL regular season play, the Thunderbirds finished with a record of 4\-5\-1\.

2015/2016: In exhibition play, the Thunderbirds went 0\-1 against Simon Fraser University, and 2\-0 against the University of Victoria\. In CWFLL regular season play, the Thunderbirds finished with a record of 9\-6\-1, on route to a CWFLL Provincial record of 5\-0, and claiming 1st place in Tier 2\.

[History](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/lacrosse/#history-352)

The UBC Thunderbirds Lacrosse Sport Club was established in 2011 by Club founder Dan Millar\. In the club’s early years of existence, the focus was on playing and teaching lacrosse for the love of the game\. In the fall of 2013, as the club became more established, it sought competition from surrounding universities in BC and Alberta\. The UBC Thunderbirds Lacrosse Sport Club finished second in their inaugural intercollegiate tournament, setting the tone for things to come\.

Traveling to the USA to compete for the first time in fall of 2013, promoting the play of intercollegiate lacrosse\. In the fall of 2014, the birds took the jump and entered the Canada West Field Lacrosse League\. Their inaugural season in the competitive league saw them achieve a record of 6\-10, a 4th place finish in the league standings, and secure a berth in the Provincial Championships\. Here, they finished as the runner\-up in the Tier II championship\. From beginning as a group of friends who agreed to pass around a ball in first year residence, UBC TSC Lacrosse has gone on to go undefeated in the 2016 season, win the 2015\-16 BC Provincial Championship, win the 2016 University of Alberta Invitational tournament, and was honored to receive the Team of the Year award at the 2015\-2016 UBC Thunderbirds Sport Club gala\. The 2018\-2019 season marked the comeback of the birds where Coach Kyle Robinson finished his last season with the Birds coaching the team to a well deserved 3rd place finish in the tier one provincials\. With high hopes and ready players, the team entered the 2019\-2020 season with a winning record under the new head coaching of beloved Connor Frost\. After a successful winter term, the team took a break that lasted longer than anyone had hope\. Despite the season being canceled, the birds kept their hands in their sticks and skills sharp, ready for the next opportunity to return to the game we all loved\. The 2021\-2022 season came fast, the team, under the head coaching of Connor Frost and Tomas Syskakis looked to rebuild and recover\. With new additions to the team, and one phenomenal goalie the team started off stronger than ever\. We played the past season giving it our all and finishing 6th in the league\.

Lacrosse really is the fastest game on two feet, it’s not just a cliché\. Lacrosse is an approachable sport, and with the knowledge of the returning players on our team, anyone can join our team and feel like a lacrosse player\.

## About the Team

The UBC Nordic Skiing TSC is a competitive ski team based out of the University of British Columbia\. At its core is a strong, accessible, and inclusive community of Nordic skiers who  
excel as competitive athletes, students, teammates, and individuals\. Throughout the academic year, the team holds regular organized practices, both on\-snow and dryland, as well as several team socials\. Off campus, the team travels to loppets and races across British Columbia and Canada to represent UBC\.

If you have any questions, please feel free to get in touch with us at [nordicski\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:nordicski.sc@ubc.ca)\!

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/nordic-skiing/#how-to-join-328)

Athletes of all skiing experiences with ambition and a commitment to improve their Nordic skiing are encouraged to get in touch with us\. For those looking to participate in practices and Loppet\-style races, prior racing experience is not required, while for those who wish to race the BC Cup Series, prior racing experience in both classic and skate skiing is expected\. All team members are encouraged to attend all practices, team socials, and events\.

Athletes interested in joining the team can contact us at [nordicski\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:nordicski.sc@ubc.ca) or find the TSC booth and Nordic Skiing Representatives on Imagine Day\. We can also be reached on social media at [@ubcnordicskiing](https://www.instagram.com/ubcnordicskiing/) for Instagram and TikTok\.

#### Eligibility Requirements:

We expect athletes to be dedicated team members and students\. Prior racing experience is not a prerequisite to join the team, but for those who want to race the BC Cup series, it is highly encouraged\. Most importantly, athletes should be highly motivated, bring a good attitude, be willing to be a part of the team community, and be able to attend practices on a weekly basis\.

Equipment Requirements:

-   Basic Running Gear
-   Properly fitted skate skis, boots, and poles
-   Properly fitted classic skis, boots, and poles
-   Basic wax setup \(glide and kick\)
-   Rollerskis optional \(helmet mandatory if choosing to rollerski\)

[Results](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/nordic-skiing/#results-330)

The start of our 2024\-25 race season kicked off in our January races where our athletes  
showcased how hard they’ve been training at Teck BC Cup 1\. For the remainder of our season,  
our athletes showed growth in both results and team camaraderie\. From going head to head  
with the best in the country at the National Championships in Canmore, to competing in the 50  
km P’ayak loppet in questionable snow conditions, it was a season for the books\. Overall, we  
came out of our race season with a female UBC sweep for the provincial university aggregates  
as well as a first place finish for the men, and approximately 5000 kilometers of collective skiing\.

We are also proud to come away from the 2024\-25 season with numerous TSC\-granted  
nominations, as well as winning the Legacy Award for graduating athlete Isaac Lowenthal  
Walsh\.

[History](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/nordic-skiing/#history-331)

Nordic skiing at UBC has had an irregular history\. From existing as an amalgamation of student\-athletes to a club, to a varsity sport in the early 2000s, to a TSC club in 2015, to an  
amalgamation of student\-athletes again in 2017, and finally to our current status as a TSC club in 2018, we have certainly undergone some changes over time\. What has remained constant is our tight\-knit community and high level of racing and performance\. Alumni still participate in races with UBC and regularly provide carpool rides to new members and rookies\. Support from community stores, clubs, and organizations such as Hollyburn and Coast Outdoors has allowed us to regularly send athletes to races near and far\. Over the years, UBC has consistently sent skiers to national championship races, as well as internationally to the United States and overseas\. In 2011, UBC’s Jesse Heckrodt attended the World University Games in Turkey, where he led the Canadian men to a 31st\-place finish\.

## About the Team

The UBC Thunderbirds Sailing Sport Club provides an opportunity for high\-level dinghy racing at the university level\. Competing in both the CICSA and ICSA conferences, the team sails against many other universities in Canada and the U\.S\. such as the University of Washington, University of Victoria, Yale University, University of Hawaii, and Tufts University\. The boats that are raced are usually dinghies like FJ’s or 420’s along with some Keel boats\.

Consistently, UBC has been top five at Canadian Dinghy Nationals and attended US Fleet Racing Nationals for five years running\. The team is thrilled to have achieved this much and hopes to keep improving in their Canadian, American, and international competitions\.

**2025\-2026 Sailing Season Information**

This year we worked hard to welcome new members and build a great team dynamic\. The team also ranked 5th out of 14 universities in the 24/25 season standings\. We attended as many events as the team could and went to regattas in places like Washington, Victoria, Toronto and Oregon\. The team worked hard to make practices, gym sessions, and events and the returning members are extremely excited for the coming season\. To ensure further success with the team we would appreciate any support\!

Feel free to email us at [sailing\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:sailing.sc@ubc.ca) or dm us on our [Instagram page](https://www.instagram.com/ubcsailing/) with any questions\.

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/sailing/#how-to-join-307)

Our athletes come from various backgrounds\. We represent many faculties such as Arts, Science, Forestry, and Engineering\. In addition, we welcome sailors of different skill levels, ranging from casual sailors looking to gain competitive experience to seasoned racers, and athletes from international backgrounds and on exchange programs\. As an inclusive group, we host various team socials to make sure all members are well adjusted and enjoying the opportunities the sailing team has to offer\. Anyone wanting to race competitively, enhance their skills with elite coaching, and join a vibrant team is encouraged to try out\.

**Eligibility Requirement:**

Sailors wanting to try out will require basic knowledge of sailing and racing\. While the team has a diverse range of beginners and experienced sailors, it is a competitive and active team representing the University of British Columbia\. We require a commitment of two practices a week, including one workout, and attendance to at least one regatta each semester\. Team fees will be outlined at the beginning of the year with inclusions outlined below\. A wetsuit and appropriate sailing gear will be required for winter practices\.

**Tryouts:** 

Tryout date will be in September and the date will be announced on our [Instagram page](https://www.instagram.com/ubcsailing/) or at our booth on [Imagine Day](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc)\!

**Team Fees:** 

Team fees are currently under review and are subject to change\. Team fees will be announced at the first info night held in September \(date will be announced on our [Instagram page](https://www.instagram.com/ubcsailing/) or at our booth on [Imagine Day](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc)\!\)

**Practice Schedule:** 

The practice season begins after **tryouts** with competition season beginning in late September and continuing until exams\.

Practice venue is at the Kitsilano Yacht Club\.

**Competition Schedule:** 

We share our competition schedule through Google Calendars, please visit that chart on our sailing home page\!

[History](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/sailing/#history-310)

The current edition of the Sailing Team branched from the AMS Sailing Club to provide a more competitive aspect for the sport at UBC in 2011\. From this transition, the team’s competitiveness grew throughout the years and by 2015 had successfully gained status as a Thunderbird Sports Club\. As a Thunderbirds Sport Club, we are now able to officially represent the university and grow within a system designed for student\-led teams to flourish\.

Although we are unsure when the AMS Sailing Club first initially originated, it has a lengthy fluctuating history with stories since 1940\.

content_markdown:
[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Artistic-Swim_Web-Banner.jpg)  

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/ArtisticSwimming-2023-TeamPhoto-scaled-wpcf_645x300.jpeg)

## About the Team

The UBC Artistic Swimming Club is a group of dedicated artistic swimmers, who are not only athletes but also students striving for excellence in both our sport and academics\. Artistic swimming, formerly known as synchronized swimming, is a blend of swimming, dance, and acrobatics\. Swimmers perform choreographed routines that merge aquatic skills with artistic performance, all while synchronizing their movements to music and each other\. This artistic sport showcases precision, grace, and teamwork in the water\.

Our club boasts multiple teams that cater to all levels of experience\. Whether you are a seasoned swimmer or someone stepping into the world of artistic swimming for the first time, you will find a welcoming and supportive environment here\. Our athletes compete within the Canadian University Artistic Swimming League \(CUASL\) at both the Western and National Championships\. In addition to swimming as a part of a team \(4\-8 swimmers\), there are also opportunities to participate in the solo, duet, and trio events\.

Join us to be part of a vibrant community that celebrates skill, dedication, and the sheer joy of artistic swimming\!

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/artistic-swimming/#how-to-join-286)

If you are interested in joining the UBC Artistic Swimming Club, we host tryouts once per year in September\. To sign up for our tryouts please fill out our [prospective athletes survey](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/prospective-athletes/)\!

If you would like to reach out to us with any questions, you can also email us at [artisticswimming\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:artisticswimming.sc@ubc.ca)\.

To keep up to date with our club follow us on Instagram [@ubcartisticswimming](https://www.instagram.com/ubcartisticswimming/)\!

**Tryouts:**

Tryouts \(as well as all of our practices\) are held at the UBC Aquatic Centre\. This year, tryouts are scheduled for the following dates:

-   Sunday, Sept\. 8th, 2024 at 8:00\-10:15 am
-   Monday, Sept\. 9th, 2024 at 7:45\-10:00 pm
-   Thursday, Sept\. 12th, 2024 at 8:00\-10:00 pm

In order to try out for our club, we ask that you attend at least two of the sessions\. The purpose of these tryouts is to assess your experience, skill level, and commitment in order for our coaches to decide which of our multiple teams is the best fit for you\.

**Try\-it Sessions:**

If you are not sure about coming to tryouts, come to our try\-it sessions\. This year we are hosting no commitment, try\-it sessions aimed specifically at people who have very little or no experience in artistic swimming\. They are scheduled for the following dates

-   Monday, Sept\. 9th, 2024 7:00\-8:00 pm
-   Thursday, Sept\. 12th, 2024 7:00\-8:00 pm

These are free sessions, where you can try artistic swimming without the stress or pressure of tryouts\. Some of our returning swimmers, and coaches will be there to guide you through some beginner skills and choreography\. These sessions are scheduled to be right before our tryouts\.

**Eligibility Requirements:**

There are two categories of artistic swimming competitions in the Canadian University Artistic Swimming League: Experienced and Novice\.

***Novice swimmers:***

-   No previous experience of artistic swimming is needed\.
-   Must be a strong swimmer, comfortable in deep water\.
-   Throughout the season, novice swimmers are required to attend 2 practices a week\.
-   Prior to the season, novice swimmers are encouraged but not required to sign up for the free trial sessions, which are intended to introduce the basic techniques of artistic swimming\.
-   For the Western and/or National championship, novice swimmers may participate in the competition as a soloist, duet, and/or team

***Experienced swimmers:***

-   Must have previously competed at a provincial or national level\.
-   Throughout the season, experienced swimmers are required to attend 3 practices a week\.
-   The tryouts held for experienced swimmers aim to assign athletes to their respective groups, depending on the athletes’ athletic ability, experience, and level of commitment\. The experienced swimmers are split up into several teams depending on how many swimmers join for the season\.
-   For the Western and/or National championship, experienced swimmers may participate in the competition as a soloist, duet, and/or team\.

\(Note: A minimum of 4 swimmers are required for team routines\)

Novice swimmers are required to attend 2 practices per week and experienced swimmers are required to attend 3 practices per week\. If you have any questions about joining our club as an experienced or novice swimmer, please contact us via email at [artisticswimming\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:artisticswimming.sc@ubc.ca)\.

**Team Fees:**

Our team fees range from $600\-900 for the year depending on the number of club members each season and your level of competition \(experienced vs\. novice\)\. Team fees include training costs, competition registration fees, and coaches’ wages\. Team fees are paid at the beginning of each term and do not typically include travel costs\. However, as a club, we do fundraisers throughout the year to cover as much of the travel cost as possible\. A more detailed breakdown of team fees will be provided at tryouts at the beginning of the season\.

**Practice Schedule:**

Practices are held at the UBC Aquatic Centre from September to mid\-March at the following times:

Novice and Experienced: Mondays & Thursdays at 8:15 – 10:00 PM

Experienced Only: Sundays at 8:15 – 10:15 AM

**Competition Schedule:**

CUASL Westerns: Calgary, AB, January 24\-26, 2025

CUASL Nationals: Victoria BC, March 21\-23, 2025

[Schedule](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/artistic-swimming/#schedule-287)

**No posts found**

[Results](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/artistic-swimming/#results-288)

In the **2023\-2024** season, our experienced and novice teams headed to Winnipeg, Manitoba for the CUASL National Championships\. There, our defending champions, the blue\-experienced team won gold in the team event with a Barbie\-themed routine, marking them as three\-time national champions\. The gold\-experienced team finished 6th with a Shrek\-themed routine, and our white\-experienced team swam exquisitely to Club music\. Furthermore, our experienced soloists secured the 2nd and 7th places, while our experienced duet won silver\. Our novice duet had an outstanding swim and placed 4th\.

In the **2022\-2023** season, at Westerns, our advanced teams were awarded 1st, 2nd and 4th, and our novice team achieved 2nd\. Our advanced extra routines also swept the podiums with our solos placing 1st, 2nd and 3rd and our duet placing 1st\. Both our novice and advanced teams traveled to Markham, Ontario for CUASL National Championships where our advanced teams placed 1st and 6th and our advanced solos took home 2nd and 5th\.

In the **2020\-2021** season, all three of our UBC Artistic Swimming duets swept the podium taking home the gold, silver and bronze at the 2021 CUASL National Championships\. Our soloist also placed first at the 2021 CUASL Nationals taking home the gold\.

In the **2019\-2020** season, our Advanced Team placed 1st at Westerns and 4th at Nationals in front of a home crowd\. Additionally, both of our Novice teams placed on the podium at Westerns taking home the silver and bronze\. The Novice Yellow Team also placed 3rd at the 2020 CUASL National Championships\. 

In the **2018\-2019** season, our Advanced Team placed 1st at Westerns and 3rd at Nationals which are now the highest rankings ever recorded for UBC Artistic Swimming\. Additionally, our Novice Team placed 1st at Westerns for the last six consecutive years, as well as 3rd at Nationals\. The Advanced Team also qualified to compete at the Canadian Artistic Swimming Championships where they placed 1st\.

[History](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/artistic-swimming/#history-289)

The UBC Artistic Swimming Club was founded over ten years ago by experienced swimmers and students as an AMS club\. Over the years, the club has grown in numbers to include a novice program, as well as expanded to include soloists and duets\.

In September 2015, the artistic swimming team, which is now composed of four teams including 2 duets and 5 soloists in the 2022/23 season, was one of the first clubs selected to become a part of the newly formed Thunderbirds Sport Clubs Program\. At the 2015 Nationals Championships, the Advanced Team won silver in the Combo category\. While the Novice Team has consecutively placed first at Westerns for the previous six years, they have also recorded second\-place finishes at the 2014 and 2016 Nationals\.

As the club has grown, swimmers have also competed in the solo and duet/trio categories\. Notably, Olivia Zawadiuk received the gold medal for her solo at the 2016 Nationals, and Olivia Zawadiuk and Katie Stirrat placed first in duet at the 2018 Nationals\.

In the 2017\-18 season, UBC Artistic Swimming made club history by having both their novice and advanced team place first at the 2018 CUASL Western Championships and UBC was able to replicate this at the 2018\-19 Westerns\. Following these performances, both the advanced and novice teams took the bronze in the team category at the 2019 CUASL National Championships  – another all\-time best for the club\.

In the 2019\-2020 season, the Advanced Gold Team once again placed first at CUASL Westerns and both Novice Teams also placed on the podium taking home the silver and bronze\. UBC Artistic Swimming also hosted the largest competition of the year, CUASL Nationals 2020 where the Novice Yellow Team placed in 3rd and the Advanced Gold Team placed in 4th\.

In the 2020\-2021 season, all 3 of our UBC Artistic Swimming duets placed on the podium taking 1st, 2nd, and 3rd at the first virtual CUASL Nationals\. Our soloist also placed first at the 2021 CUASL Nationals taking home the gold\.

In the 2021\-2022 season, UBC Artistic Swimming had their first CUASL National championship win in history and were also awarded the Gerry Dubrule Trophy for the top overall university as well as the John Drake Trophy for the top experienced team\.

In the 2022\-2023 season, UBC Artistic Swimming travelled to their first in\-person competition in Markham, Ontario after the pandemic and brought home the John Drake Trophy for the top experienced team for the second consecutive year\.

In the 2023\-2024 season, UBC Artistic Swimming headed to a competition in Winnipeg, Manitoba and brought home the John Drake Trophy for the top experienced team for three consecutive years and one of our experienced swimmers brought home the title of the Top Experienced Athlete\.

[Additional Information](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/artistic-swimming/#additional-information-291)

In early December, we will be showcasing our training progress with a “Winter Water Show”\. Additionally, we will also be performing our final routines at the end of our season, the “Year End Water Show” in early March before we depart for the CUASL National Championship\.

Additionally, throughout the year, our club will be holding numerous fundraisers, such as Krispy Kreme, Bak’d cookies, and many more\. Stay tuned for more information\!

## About the Team

The UBC Men’s tennis team is a highly competitive member of the Thunderbirds Sports Clubs \(TSC\), winning the 2022 Canadian University Tennis Championship\. The team participates at the highest rank of University tennis in Canada, competing against teams from across the country\. Tryouts are held each year to keep the team competitive and to bring fresh players to the roster\. The competitive season starts mid\-February and ends in August with the Canadian National Championships, held alongside the Rogers Cup\. Our goal is to earn a spot at the Canadian National Championships and bring home a national championship for UBC\.

For recruitment, donations, sponsorships, or any other inquiries please email us at [menstennis\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:menstennis.sc@ubc.ca)

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/tennis-m/#how-to-join-265)

Tryouts for the 2022/2023 season are now open\. Barring any unforeseen circumstances, we will be holding in\-person tryouts for the 2022/2023 season on Monday, September 12th from 7:30\-9:30 pm\.

If you’re interested in joining the team for the 2022/2023 season please sign up [here](https://l.instagram.com/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.google.com%2Fspreadsheets%2Fd%2F1wn5gDlDRBNeTYCOT-rRu6A_kP1TVOwSsbes_frRsgaQ%2Fedit&e=ATMSB59NRTesrSoTZzSO_hGp613BQ_0ssE_hOeVpCzDudW4q343IDWHp3bCyYWR5A3aA3haE0GPRtqvmhz72LOUFnB_LgQ2g4fSSsQ&s=1)\. If you have any questions in the meantime, please email us at [menstennis\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:menstennis.sc@ubc.ca)

**Why You Should Join:**

The team comprises of 12 students each year, who are extremely passionate and determined to both better their game, and bring success to the team\. Each year we look for new players who will match our drive and spirit to elevate our collective results to new levels\. We invite anyone who is interested to try out for the team\. Through tough practices, tight competitions, and traveling, the team bonds together creating lifelong memories and relationships\. We are an extremely tight\-knit group of players, always supporting one another whether it be in sport or in each other’s academic journeys\.

**Eligibility Requirements:**

The current team members maintain a high and competitive level of tennis\. Previous experience in both practice and match situations is highly recommended for prospective players\. What we expect of all UBC Men’s Tennis student\-athletes throughout the season:

-   Attendance of all 3 weekly practices
-   Attendance at all competitions such as; Provincials, Westerns, Nationals, friendly matches
-   Attendance at all fundraising events such as; Tennis Mixer, etc\.
-   Best effort and attitude at all competitions, practices, etc\.

**Team Fees:** 

Team fees vary depending on the number of competitions, roster sizes, fundraising, etc\. Fees generally range between $50 to $150 per term, plus a mandatory \~$120 fee for our team apparel\. Exact costs will be determined at the start of the season and will be announced well in advance\.

**Practice Schedule:**

-   *\(2x\)* 2\-hr weeknight on\-court practice at the UBC Tennis Centre
-   *\(1x\)* 2\-hr weekend on\-court practice at the UBC Tennis Centre

*\*Exact days and times will be provided once the roster is established, to accommodate all student\-athletes\.*

**Competition Schedule:**

The competition schedule will be determined at a later time\.

*\*All dates, times, matches and the National Championships will be determined at a later time \(TBD\)*

## About the Team

*\(header image: [Kevin LeClaire, Ultiphotos](https://www.ultiphotos.com/usau/college/d1/champs/2023/teams)\)*

The UBC Thunderbirds Women’s Ultimate Sport Club is a consistently high\-performing team that competes primarily in the USA Ultimate \(USAU\) College Series in the spring of each school year with the primary goal of qualifying for – and winning – the USA College National Championships\.

Regular seasons begin with tryouts happening in October/November and continue with regular practices happening from the beginning of January until the end of May\. Regular season tournaments typically occur in March, qualifier tournaments in April, and National Championships in May\.

We are so excited to be back for the 2025\-2026 season\! Keep your eyes out on this website and our team Instagram [@ubcwultimate](https://www.instagram.com/ubcwultimate/?hl=en) to stay up to date\.

Contact us with any questions through [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/ubcwultimate/?hl=en) or [email](mailto:womensultimate.sc@ubc.ca)\!

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/ultimate-w/#how-to-join-244)

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/ActionShot-WUltimate-360x238.jpg)

The UBC Thunderbirds Women’s Ultimate Sport Club is looking for passionate and skilled players to join our 2025\-2026 team\. Ultimate is a unique sport that combines athleticism, skill, and spirit; and we value all three aspects of the game\. We pride ourselves in promoting an inclusive and fun atmosphere without sacrificing our competitive drive to be one of the top 5 ranked Women’s Ultimate teams in North America\. We invite all students interested in competing at high\-level women’s ultimate to come to our try\-outs\.

Our tryout form for the 2025\-2026 season will be posted later in September\.

**Eligibility Requirements:**

Previous experience with the sport will be an asset, although is not necessarily required to make the team\. There is an expectation that players will do their best effort to attend all three practices a week \(two evenings and one weekend morning\) and all tournaments\. Athletes will also be expected to complete required additional individual fitness outside of practice\. Lastly, athletes will be required to have a valid passport in order to travel to the United States regularly for tournament play\.

**Equipment Requirements**

The Ultimate player’s mantra when leaving the house: “Light, dark, cleats, water”\.

**Tryouts:** 

Dates: TBA

The first tryout will be an open tryout, then the last two will be closed to help better select the team for this year\.

**Team Fees:** 

Regular season: Team fees will be paid in installments throughout the spring and will roughly total to $700\-$800\. This cost will cover fields, tournament fees, hotels, etc\. Certain tournaments will require flying \(Stanford Invite and Nationals\) and are the individual responsibility of the player\. They will add to roughly $1000\-1200 total\. There will be significant fundraising efforts made throughout the season to help subsidize these costs\.

**Practice Schedule:**

Practices will start in November and continue until the end of May, leading up to Nationals\. There will be two to three practices per week spanning 2 hours each session\.

-   Two practices will take place on weeknight evenings \(7\-9 pm or 8\-10 pm\) and
-   One practice will take place Saturday mornings: time TBA\.

The exact time and locations will depend on field assignments for the month\.

**Competition Schedule:**

To be announced\!

[History](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/ultimate-w/#history-247)

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/WUltimate-2008Champions-e1499459904839-360x212.jpg)

Founded in 1997, the Women’s Ultimate team has competed yearly in the USAU College Series and holds a National Championship Title from 2008\. A high level of achievement has been maintained over the years, with a 5th place finish in 2016 and 2022, 3rd place finishes in 2015, 2017, and 2023\.

The team consistently is ranked among the top teams in North America and seems to have an endless flow of young talent from the Junior Ultimate Programs in BC\. Vancouver has a strong junior ultimate scene which has provided a talented pipeline for the UBC team\. In fact, many rookies join the team with years of high\-level playing experience already under their belt, be it with Team BC or Team Canada\. Many UBC players have represented Canada at U20 and U23 junior worlds in the past, bringing home bronze, silver, and gold medals\. UBC leads the country in the growth of elite women’s Ultimate, with the current 2023 U24 Canadian team being represented by many Thunderbirds as well\.

Beyond the many players who have competed on the U19 and U23 Canadian National Teams, UBC’s distinguished alumni Candice Chan, Mira Donaldson, Catherine Hui, Kira Frew, Rena Kawabata, and Rachel Moens have all competed for the Canadian World Games Team, playing at the highest level on the world stage\.

There is a subsequent fee of $25 for locker cleaning and storage that must be paid prior to obtaining belongings\.

## Welcome to UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs

The UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs \(UBC TSC\) is a competitive sport program for UBC student\-athletes\. UBC TSC is home to fifteen sports and seventeen teams which include:

-   Alpine Skiing
-   Artistic Swimming
-   Curling
-   Cycling
-   Equestrian
-   Field Lacrosse
-   Nordic Skiing
-   Quadball
-   Sailing

-   Squash
-   Table Tennis
-   Men’s Tennis
-   Women’s Tennis
-   Triathlon
-   Men’s Ultimate
-   Women’s Ultimate
-   Wrestling

TSC student athletes get to experience representing UBC in competition locally, across Canada and in the United States\. Following a pay\-to\-play model, Sport Clubs provide the opportunity for students to be part of a team, build community, develop leadership skills and train for the sport they love\!

## UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs

UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs \(TSC\) within the Department of Athletics and Recreation, is a competitive sport clubs program that features 13 sports, 15 teams, and over 330 student\-athletes\. Launched in 2015, these student\-led sport clubs represent UBC in competitions across Canada and the United States\.

As a competitive program, all teams participate in club or intercollegiate leagues at a local, provincial, national, or international level\. Each Sport Club must be financially self\-sustaining, supporting their operations through fundraising, sponsorship, athlete dues, and funding from the Department of Athletics and Recreation for coaching, National Championship travel, and competitive enhancement\.

In the pursuit of becoming the leading competitive sport clubs program in Canada, UBC takes pride in supporting the development of its employees, student executives, and athletes\. The Sport Clubs Office provides comprehensive student leadership training to equip executives with the skills, knowledge, and resources to successfully operate their clubs\.

## About Thunderbirds Sport Clubs

In 2013\-14, UBC conducted a Sport Review to ensure the long term sustainability of competitive athletics at UBC\. As a result of this review, 26 sports were designated as Varsity programs, while a new stream of competitive sport was added to provide additional opportunities for student athletes to represent UBC as Thunderbirds\. This new stream officially launched in 2015\-16 as the Thunderbirds Sport Clubs Program \(TSC\)\.

Since the inception of the program, UBC Sport Clubs have achieved considerable competitive success, including numerous national championships \(Artistic Swimming, 2022, 2023, 2024; Men's Tennis, 2022, 2024; Triathlon, 2024, 2025; Women's Ultimate, 2025\), multiple podium finishes at national championships, and numerous athletes representing their country at the international level\.

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/AR_SportBreakdown-768x266.png)

Each Sport Club is built on three key pillars:

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Screen-Shot-2018-06-07-at-9.02.43-AM.png)

## Frequently Asked Questions

[**How do Sport Clubs compare to Varsity teams?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/about/#how-do-sport-clubs-compare-to--236)

Although Sport Clubs and Varsity student\-athletes may have similar health and competitive sport goals, UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs are completely *student\-driven* and compete in sports not already offered within the varsity program at UBC\. Thunderbirds Sport Clubs may have professional coaches and receive administrative and financial support from UBC Athletics and Recreation, however, each club is fully operated by its student leaders\. These students are tasked with administrative, financial, and social responsibilities for their respective teams, which include scheduling games and tournaments, handling practices and facility rentals, fundraising, organizing competition travel, and hiring coaches \- just to name a few\. Sport Club executives and athletes are presented with an excellent opportunity to build leadership, teamwork, and professional skills that can launch their careers after their time at UBC\.

[**How do Sport Clubs compare to AMS Clubs?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/about/#how-do-sport-clubs-compare-to--237)

While Thunderbirds Sport Clubs and AMS Clubs focus on student leadership and development, UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs strives for *competitive excellence*\. With weekly practices, Sport Clubs travel locally, nationally, and internationally to compete against other universities, representing UBC at a highly competitive level\. Sport Clubs athletes are challenged with athletic and self\-development, enriching their experiences at the University\.

[**How do Sport Clubs compare to Intramurals?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/about/#how-do-sport-clubs-compare-to--238)

With student leadership driving the Sport Clubs and Intramurals programs, UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs allows students to compete at an inter\-collegiate level\. Sport Clubs encourage athletes to be competitive and successful within their athletic domains, while Intramurals allow athletes to try out new sports at the recreational level\. For athletes looking for a balance between competition and recreation, Sport Clubs provide the perfect in\-between\.

[**My sport is not listed, can I still get involved?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/about/#my-sport-is-not-listed-can-i-s-239)

UBC Athletics and Recreation will review current sport club programs and will accept applications for the TSC program approximately every two years\.

**If an AMS Club for your sport exists**, we suggest you get involved in the competitive component of their club or the creation of their competitive component\.

**If an AMS Club for your sport does *not* exist**, we highly suggest you create an AMS Club to prepare for your TSC application\.

If you run a highly competitive team on campus and would like to take this next step, please email your inquiries to [sport\.clubs@ubc\.ca](mailto:sport.clubs@ubc.ca)\.

[**Am I eligible to be a TSC Athlete?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/about/#am-i-eligible-to-be-a-tsc-athl-240)

To be a Sport Clubs athlete, UBC requires each athlete to be registered in 9 credits per term or registered in a UBC\-affiliated co\-op term\. \(A player can be registered in fewer than 9 credits if they have fulfilled all their academic requirements and are expecting to graduate in that term\.\) In addition, they must maintain a cumulative average of 60% in order to remain eligible for athlete status\.

[**I am a UBC Okanagan Student, how can I participate?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/about/#i-am-a-ubc-okanagan-student-ho-241)

While the above teams are only available to UBC Vancouver Students, there are Sport Clubs available at UBC Okanagan\. Head to their home page for more information: [UBC Okanagan Recreational Sport Clubs](https://recreation.ok.ubc.ca/sports/sport-clubs/)

[**How do I get more information about a club or TSC in general?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/about/#how-do-i-get-more-information--242)

If you would like more information on getting involved with UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs, either on an existing team or for a new sport, please contact the team directly through their team email or email [sport\.clubs@ubc\.ca](mailto:sport.clubs@ubc.ca) for general inquiries\.

[**Club Application Process**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/about/#club-application-process-243)

The most recent application process for the UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs program took place in the Fall of 2025\. The next opportunity to apply for the program will be no earlier than 2027\.

For more information please refer to the [TSC Applications \- 2019 Information Package](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/TSC-Applications-2019-Information-Package.pdf)\.

### *Student Driven\. Competitive Excellence\. One Community\.* 

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/FeaturedImage-TSC-Crop.jpg)

Interested in joining the UBC community as an official Sport Club student\-athlete at the UBC Vancouver campus? Thunderbirds Sport Clubs \(TSC\) is a great opportunity to connect with other students who are passionate about your sport, or previously played while growing up\. Excelling on the field, in the classroom, and in the campus community is encouraged\.

Each individual Sport Club hosts tryouts every year, typically in September\. Connect with specific teams via email or keep an eye on each club’s page for updates on tryouts\.

Although previous experience is an asset, we encourage those who would like to try something new to contact the team executives for more information\. If you make the team you also have the opportunity to hold various executive positions in each club\.

[**TSC Eligibility Requirements**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/prospective-athletes/#tsc-eligibility-requirements-232)

Students who wish to compete in the UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs stream must first be accepted to UBC based on faculty requirements\. Athletes are then expected to meet the following requirements:

-   Enrolled in a minimum of nine \(9\) credits per term at UBC Vancouver
-   Maintain enrollment in the minimum number of credits for the entirety of each session
-   Achieve and maintain good academic standing or passing standards \(minimum 60%\)
-   Meet the requirements of a Co\-op, Masters, or PhD\. student during their work term \(if applicable\)
-   Attend the Mandatory Athlete Orientation
-   Possess AMS or Personal Insurance
-   Complete and submit the appropriate Sport Clubs Forms

[**How much time is dedicated to a team per week?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/prospective-athletes/#how-much-time-is-dedicated-to--233)

The amount of time dedicated to practices and games will often vary per team, however expect on average two \(2\) practices per week and a tournament/game on weekends\.

Example Schedules:

Practices from 9:00 \- 10:30 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays, Games on Saturday nights at 8:00 pm, Team gym sessions on Sunday evenings from 7:00 \- 8:30 pm\. Total \= a minimum of 7 hours per week**\.**

Those interested in holding executive positions on Sport Club teams should expect an additional 5\-10 hours of responsibilities aside from practice/gym times and games\.

[**Do Sport Club teams travel for competition?**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/prospective-athletes/#do-sport-club-teams-travel-for-234)

The majority of UBC Thunderbirds Sport Club teams travel across North America for many of their competitions against other schools or club teams\. Locations include:

-   Vancouver and the Lower Mainland
-   British Columbia
-   Other Provinces in Canada
-   United States \(primarily in the Central or NW coast of the States\)

In 2017\-18 some teams travelled to Victoria \(BC\), Edmonton \(AB\), Kingston \(ON\), Lake Placid \(NY\), Seattle \(WA\), Milwaukee \(WI\), and Fremont \(CA\), just to name a few places\.

[**I am an International or Exchange Student**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/home/prospective-athletes/#i-am-an-international-or-excha-235)

We encourage all students at UBC \- Domestic, International, or Exchange students to participate in UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs\! If you are arriving at UBC in Term 2 \(January\), please contact the specific Sport Club Executives regarding tryouts or playing for the team\.

Fill out the form below if you are interested in hearing more about any of our Thunderbirds Sport Clubs teams\. This form will not add you to the team but will send the information you provide to the student executives who run that respective TSC team\. If you are interested in multiple teams, please submit a different form for each team\.

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/Cycling-3.png)

## About the Team

The UBC Thunderbirds Cycling Sport Club is a competitive road cycling team competing in the local Vancouver race series and the USA Cycling Northwest Collegiate Cycling Conference \(NWCCC\)\.

We aim to develop riders into competitive, safe, and smart racers to form a high\-ranking team capable of winning elite races\. The collegiate season extends from April to June, although team members compete in races throughout the summer and fall\.

The essence of the UBC Thunderbirds Cycling Sport Club is fueled by team members’ shared passion for cycling and the community around this spectacular sport\. We provide an introduction to safe riding, developing key technical skills, and learning how to win races\. 

**Sponsors:**

We are currently in the process of finding sponsors for the 2025/2026 season\. If you are interested in becoming a sponsor please email us at cycling\.sc@ubc\.ca\.

Last year, our 2024/2025 team was sponsored by [Choose Health YVR](https://www.choose.health/), [Fist Bump Filmworks](https://www.fistbumpfilmworks.com/), [SOLE](https://yoursole.com/ca), [UBC Bike Kitchen](https://www.thebikekitchen.ca/), [BICI](https://bici.cc/), [Fasttrack Auto Body](https://www.fastrackautobody.com/), [raceworx](https://www.raceworx.ca/), [Myodetox](https://www.myodetox.com/locations/canada/british-columbia/vancouver/), [UBC REC](https://linkin.bio/ubcrec/) and [UBC TSC](https://linktr.ee/ubctsc)\. We would like to extend a sincere thank you to all of our sponsors\!

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/cycling-sc/#how-to-join-211)

The UBC Thunderbirds Cycling Sport Club provides an opportunity for athletes to compete in high\-level sport while granting new riders a comprehensive immersion into the sport of cycling\. 

#### **Eligibility Requirements:**

No past racing experience is required\. We are looking for hard\-working riders with good attitudes\. Please ensure that you have the right equipment \(drop bar road bike with skinny tires and working gears\)\.

Members are required to fulfill the following:

-   Full\-time student \(minimum 9 credits per semester\)
-   Weekly Saturday rides during the Winter session at 9 AM at Thunderbird Stadium\. \(NOTE: Athletes must be rostered after tryouts to attend group rides\.\)
-   Additional weekly training sessions
-   Members will need a valid passport and UCI Race License in order to compete in the USA\. \(Note: Do not purchase a new race license until after January 1st for racing in 2025\.\)

#### **Tryouts:** 

The 2025/2026 team will be capped at around 26 athletes\. Tryouts will be based on an athlete’s level of commitment to the team and general athleticism\. We expect all members to ride safely and to follow the rules of the road\. Attendance at weekly Saturday rides and completion of the required training sessions will be key factors in making the team\.

Although we look for cycling ability, we also focus on prospective development and contribution to a positive team environment\. We are scoping for athletes who are eager and capable of competing come race season\.

2025/2026 season try out dates:

-   September 13th \(Open ride, not part of try outs, but we encourage you to attend\!\)
-   September 20th \(Try outs 1, open to all\)
-   September 27th \(Try outs 2, only if invited\)

Feel free to contact us at cycling\.sc@ubc\.ca if you have any questions\.

#### **Team Fees:**

The 2025/2026 Team Fees are subject to change\. If these fees pose a barrier to you joining our team, please get in touch with us as soon as possible\.

-   TSC Athlete Membership fee: $100 \(One time fee\)
-   Team Fee: $100 per term \(Tehe funding from team fees goes directly back into athlete’s racing\)
-   Cost of team kit: TBD \(It will be at a reduced team rate\)

#### **Training Schedule:**

Weekly Saturday morning team rides at 9 AM leaving from Thunderbird Stadium from September through April\. The ride usually lasts 3 to 5 hours\. Additional indoor and outdoor training sessions will be optional during the week\. There are no mandatory group rides over stat holidays, reading week or exam period\.

#### **Competition Schedule:**

Our competition schedule is comprised of both local and collegiate racing\. Local racing begins in March and occurs almost every weekend till the end of June\. The Vancouver racing scene is competitive and growing, making for tight and fun racing\!

The collegiate series will take place from April to June\. Races are around 1 to 13 hours driving distance from Vancouver, depending on the host\. For out\-of\-town races, the team will usually depart from Vancouver on Fridays \(often later in the day if possible, to allow for members to attend their classes or work\), and drive back after races finish on Sunday morning\. A collegiate weekend includes a road race and team time trial on Saturday and a criterium on Sunday morning\.

Only races held during the school year will be mandatory to attend, although summer racing is strongly encouraged\!  

#### **Academic Requirements:**

Team members must maintain good academic standing – minimum 60% average or passing standards as identified by their faculty – and must not be on academic probation\.

Team members must be students at the University of British Columbia who are registered in an Undergraduate or Graduate 9\-credit course load per term in the current winter session, or fulfilling the requirements for a PhD/Masters, or Co\-op Program\. \(Students registered in diploma programs, certificate programs, or affiliated colleges/ programs with the University of British Columbia including Carey Theological College, Regent College, St\. Mark’s College, and the Vancouver School of Theology, are not eligible for active membership in a UBC Thunderbirds Sport Club\.\)

#### **Interest Form:**

Interested in joining the team? Please complete the following [form](https://linktr.ee/ubccycling?lt_utm_source=lt_share_link#502205576) so we can contact you during our recruiting period in September 2025\.

**Non\-Collegiate Results:**

2016 USA Hill Climb Nationals – Bronze – Margot Clyne  
Colorado State Road Champion \(SW 1\-2\) – Margot Clyne  
2017 USA Hill Climb National Champion – Margot Clyne

[History](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/cycling-sc/#history-214)

As a part of the UBC AMS Bike Club, our team dates back to the 1990’s but was revived after many years of dormancy\. Following the return of the competitive side of the club in 2014, it has gone from just a handful of riders to more than twenty racers since 2015\. 

The 2016\-17 season marked our inaugural year as a competitive sport club with UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs\. The club has seen better overall standings since joining TSC\. We have moved from 6th to 3rd, to 4th place in the end\-of\-season team standings in the NWCCC over the past years\. The 2017\-2018 season had several notable accomplishments including holding 2nd place overall in the team omnium for several weeks and winning the Men’s B and Women’s C omniums\. 

Former Club Lead and alumnus Margot Clyne transitioned from competing for UBC Cycling to riding with a professional women’s race team\. She was pivotal in our establishment as a Thunderbird Sport Club and brought together our strong women’s team\.

Throughout the last seven years, the team has continued to grow into one of the key development cycling teams in the North\-West, preparing athletes to continue on to elite racing teams\. In 2025, the team won the mixed\-team category at the Whistler Grand Fondo to round off a year of many successes in all disciplines and categories\.

## About the Team

The UBC Thunderbirds Equestrian Sport Club trains out of Riverside Equestrian Centre and competes in the Intercollegiate Horse Show Association \(IHSA\)\. We are part of Zone 8, Region 4 and we compete mostly in Washington and Oregon, USA\. UBC is the only Western University of the 7 Canadian Universities in the IHSA, which totals 419 teams across North America\. The Equestrian team is currently showing in the Hunt Seat sector of the IHSA\. In the 2024\-2025  
season, the team proudly expanded to include a new Intercollegiate Dressage Association \(IDA\) section – marking its debut in this riding discipline\. At these shows, horses are donated for use by their owners and assigned at random to determine rider/horse pairings\. Riders compete in both flat and jumping classes in a true test of skill and horsemanship\.

Showing in the IHSA provides students with a unique equestrian experience throughout their University careers\. Riders’ abilities and divisions range from complete beginners to advanced athletes, creating a space for all levels while sharing the same love and passion for the sport\. Our team gives students the opportunity to travel and build team relationships with other student riders, as we engage in practices, activities, and of course, the shows\. We also value our strong friendships developed while on the team through our social events, and cheer one another on in the ring\.

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/equestrian-sc/#how-to-join-190)

**Tryouts:** 

Tryouts will be held in a bi\-partisan system\! Follow us on Instagram [@ubcequestrianteam](https://www.instagram.com/ubcequestrianteam/?hl=en) for updates as they are released\!

**Lessons:** 

Lessons are starting in late September/early October and will run throughout Term 1 and Term 2\.

**Eligibility Requirements:** 

The IHSA has 8 levels of hunt seat riding, from the Walk\-Trot flat class to Open over fences\. Since our show format is catch riding, \(i\.e\. we do not get warm\-up time before our judged round or flat class, and usually have never ridden the horses before\) we recommend some previous riding experience even for the beginner divisions\. The more practice riders are able to get on different horses, the better they will become at showing IHSA\. To be eligible for our IHSA Hunt Seat Team, riders must be enrolled in a full\-time undergraduate program at UBC and in good academic standing\.

Team members will be required to ride weekly with our team coach at Riverside, attend monthly meetings, compete in at least 3 competitions, and participate in TSC Equestrian fundraisers and events\. Riders are responsible for their own basic show attire: black tall boots, tan breeches, white show shirt, black or navy hunter show jacket, and black riding helmet\.

**Team Fees:** 

Just like any competitive sport, there are costs to pay\. However, the amounts of each fee change year to year depending on the number of riders on the team\. We also try our best to keep these fees as low as possible by hosting fundraisers throughout the year\!

As a new member, one can expect the following costs throughout the year:

-   Tryout fee
-   Team fee
-   IHSA membership fee
-   Term lesson fees
-   Apparel fee \(optional\)
-   Show fees \(vary depending on your division and travel costs\)

**Practice Schedule:**

Athletes are required to ride weekly at Riverside Equestrian Centre with our coach Natalie Adler\. If students already have a hunter/jumper/equitation coach in the Vancouver area, they may request an exemption from weekly lessons at Riverside but must still ride once per month in the UBC program\.

**Competition Schedule:**

The Team will be competing in the 2025\-2026 season\.

[History](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/equestrian-sc/#history-193)

UBC Equestrian was previously an AMS Club with a competitive component\. The AMS Club still exists as an equestrian community at UBC, but no longer contains the IHSA show team\. The 2015\-2016 season was the first year our team qualified for IHSA Regional, Zone, and National finals\.

[Additional Information](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/equestrian-sc/#additional-information-195)

**Levels of Competition:**  
Intercollegiate Horse Show Association

Class 1: Introductory Hunter Seat Equitation  
Walk\-Trot riders are those who have had no more than 24 weeks of instruction and who have not competed in a mounted competition that required them to canter\. Diagonals will count\.

Class 2A: Pre\-Novice Hunter Seat Equitation  
Class 2B: Novice Hunter Seat Equitation  
Eligible for class 2A are those who have had more than 24 weeks of instruction and who have not competed in a mounted competition that required them to jump more than eighteen inches\. Leads and diagonals count\. 2B riders have not competed in any over fences classes higher than three feet in any competition, nor competed in any recognized competitions\.

Class 3: Limit Hunter Seat Equitation  
Those who have won no more than five Hunter Seat equitation classes on the flat in recognized competitions\.

Class 4: Limit Hunter Seat Equitation Over Fences  
Novice riders over fences have won no more than six classes in any over fences class three feet \(3’\) or higher in recognized competitions\. Riders must have had at least six months continuous professional instruction over fences within the past year\. To be shown over six or more fences at least 2′ 3″ in height and not to exceed 2′ 9″, and including at least one change of direction\.

Class 5: Intermediate Hunter Seat Equitation  
Intermediate riders on the flat are those who have won six to ten Hunter Seat equitation classes on the flat in recognized competitions\.

Class 6: Intermediate Hunter Seat Equitation Over Fences  
Intermediate riders over fences have won no more than six classes in any over fences class three feet, six inches \(3’6”\) or higher in recognized competitions\.To be shown over six or more fences at least 2′ 6″ in height and not to exceed 3′, including at least one change of direction\.

Class 7: Open Hunter Seat Equitation  
Open riders on the flat are those who have won more than ten Hunter Seat equitation classes on the flat in recognized competitions\.

Class 8: Open Hunter Seat Equitation Over Fences  
Open riders over fences are those who have won more than six classes in any over fences class three feet, six inches \(3’6”\) or higher in recognized competitions\. To be shown over six or more fences at least 2′ 9″ in height and not to exceed 3′ 3″ in height and 3′ in width including at least one change of direction\.

Intercollegiate Dressage Association  
Levels of Competition:  
Introductory Level \(Intro A & B\):  
Minimum Qualifications: This level is designed for beginning dressage riders that have a  
minimum of 12 hours of riding instruction within 1 year prior to competing in the IDA  
Maximum Qualificantions: Riders have maximum 2 \-year calendar limit to compete at this level  
dating from their joining the IDA\.  
\*Note: Introductory riders must be reclassified each year of their two\-year eligibility with the same qualifications of a new rider

Lower Training:  
1\. Intro C  
2\. Training Level Test 1

Upper Training:  
1\. Training Level Test 2  
2\. Training Level Test 3

First Level: Riders who exceed qualifications of the intro, lower training, and upper training  
divisions

## About the Team

UBC TSC Quadball is a competitive team with a year\-long season\. Based on the sport of Quidditch from the “Harry Potter” series, Quadball blends elements of rugby, dodgeball, handball, and even flag football, for an intense and exciting experience\. Quadball is the only sport that is fully co\-ed as well as being full contact\. We compete with other teams from all over Canada as well as the northwestern US\.

Quadball is an incredible and worthwhile sport on its own merits, regardless of its origins in Harry Potter\. What makes it really stand apart from other sports is the community and culture\. While everyone in our club takes the sport seriously and takes our training and performance seriously, off the pitch it is an amazingly different environment from what most people experience in traditional sports\. UBC Thunderbirds Quadball Sport Club attracts players who create a culture that is inclusive and accepting\. We’re looking for a unique mix of athleticism, academics, open, and social individuals; and those who don’t mind tackling others every now and then\.

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/quidditch-sc/#how-to-join-184)

Quadball is a fun way to get in shape, make new friends, travel and compete against other universities\. We also have many social events such as the Yule Ball and Rookie Night\! We welcome all students who would love to join our Thunderbirds Sport Club team and compete as an official UBC student athlete\. For more information please feel free to contact an executive member at [quidditch\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:quidditch.sc@ubc.ca)\.

We post information about our tryouts and open practices where you can try out the sport on our Instagram [@ubcquadball](https://www.instagram.com/ubcquadball/) or Facebook [@ubctscquadball\.](https://www.facebook.com/ubctscquadball)

**Eligibility Requirements:**

-   Attend all team practices, games and gym sessions
-   Notify Coach of all conflicts and absences 2 weeks in advance
-   Must pay team and tournament fees
-   Must be a full\-time UBC Student \(typically this means 9 credits a term, however, co\-op and exchange students are also eligible\!\)
-   Must be in good academic standing\. Must maintain an average of over 60% in order to compete or travel, but lower can still train with the team\.

**Tryouts:** 

Interested in learning more about quadball? Come check out our booth on Imagine Day \(September 3rd\) or come to our fun try\-quadball nights in September to try out for the team\.

-   **Try\-Quadball Nights** – Open for all and will include fun games that build skills for quadball and a minigame to get a feel for the game\.
    -   These are very informal and we do not expect players to already know how to play\! Just bring a positive attitude and eagerness to learn\.
    -   To our Try\-it nights please bring shoes you can run in, a water bottle, and comfortable clothing\. We provide the rest 🙂

**Team Fees:**

Team fees will be around $250 CAD per semester \(subject to change, hopefully will be lower\)\. These fees will cover your uniform, field rentals, equipment usage, travel insurance, travel costs, tournament fees and social events\.

We expect every member of our team to help with fundraising efforts, any excess funds we have will be reimbursed to members\.

**Practice Schedule:**

-   We will have 2 practices a week in Term 1 and 2 and optional team gym hours for TSC athletes once a week\.
    -   We will have one indoor practice and one outdoor practice per week\.
    -   Our outdoor practices will be on Mondays from 7\-9pm on MacInnes Field\.
-   We will have weekly TSC gym hours in Term 1 and 2, on Sunday Nights from 7\-8:30pm at Birdcoop Gym\.
-   We will also have social events throughout the term, so there will be no shortage of activities\!

**Competition Schedule:**

-   We aim to attend or host one local tournament a month\. Some tournaments for the following year include:
    -   UBC October Octopus Open Tournament
    -   Western Divisionals \(at UBC\)
    -   Canadian Nationals
    -   UBC Hosted Tournament
    -   Vancouver Quadball Cup

[History](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/quidditch-sc/#history-187)

The UBC Quadball Club was founded in 2010 as an AMS Club\. UBC Quadball plays in the Canadian league \(Quidditch Canada\) and is a UBC Thunderbirds Sport Club\.

Perennially, UBC Quadball is often one of the strongest teams in BC and most of its surrounding area, with victories against teams all over BC and Washington\. We have been battling to be the best team in Western Canada against the Alberta Clippers, SFU Quidditch, and Vancouver Vanguard Quidditch for over 12 years\.

In January 2023, Quidditch Canada changed the sport’s name to Quadball and our sport club followed suit\.
