## About the Team

The UBC Women’s Tennis Team is a nationally competitive Thunderbirds Sport Club \(TSC\) and competes in the U Sports division of University sports, the highest rank of University Tennis in Canada\. The ultimate goal of the UBC Women’s Tennis SC for the upcoming season is to earn a place at the Canadian National Championships, held in August of 2026, alongside the Rogers Cup in Toronto or Montreal\. The competitive season begins at the start of 2026, however, pre\-season training and competition starts in September 2025\.

If you are interested in trying out for the 2025\-26 season, we will hold open tryouts in September 2025\. As September approaches, check out our [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/ubcwtennis/?hl=en) feed to find out the exact date of registration and tryouts; make sure you don’t miss it\! We look forward to seeing some new faces\.

For recruitment, general inquiries, or donation inquiries please email us at [womenstennis\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:womenstennis.sc@ubc.ca)\.

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/tennis-w/#how-to-join-52)

**Why You Should Join:**

The UBC Women’s Tennis SC is made up of about 12\-16 student\-athletes who all share a passion for the sport of tennis and who wish to compete in women’s tennis to represent UBC\. New players who share the team’s passion and will add positively to the team are always welcome\. We invite all students who are interested in competing at a high level in tennis to come to tryouts in September at the beginning of each academic year\. Joining the UBC TSC Women’s Tennis Team enables a player to both improve within the sport and build long\-lasting relations within the team\. The tight\-knit and supportive players are encouraging and motivating\. Although tennis is known to be an individual sport, the UBC TSC Women’s Tennis Team creates a true team atmosphere, as everyone works together to achieve the same goal\.

**Eligibility Requirements:**

The current team members maintain a high and competitive level of tennis\. Therefore, previous experience is highly recommended in both practice and match situations for prospective players\. Interested players are always welcome to try out in September for the upcoming season\.

Expectations for the women’s tennis student\-athletes throughout the season include:

-   Attendance of three practices per week
-   Attendance at all competitions, such as: Regionals, Westerns, Nationals \(if the team qualifies\), and other season matches
-   Attendance at all fundraising events, such as: October Tennis Mixer and possibly others
-   Best effort and attitude at all competitions, practices, and other events

**Team Fees:**

Team fees will vary depending on the number of competitions, roster size, and fundraising, but are expected to be between $50 to $200 per term, and about $100 for a mandatory, one\-time, competition apparel fee\.

\*Fees will be determined at a later time\.

**Practice Schedule:**

-   2 x two\-hour weeknight on\-court practice
-   1 x two\-hour weekend on\-court practice

\*On\-court practices may include some strength and conditioning sessions\.

\*\*Days and times will be decided once the roster is established to best accommodate all student\-athletes\.

**Competition Schedule:**

-   November: Fall Match against University of Calgary; away
-   November: Fall Match against University of Alberta; away
-   January: UBC Team vs Team BC Juniors; home
-   January: UVIC Invitational Tournament \(\*UBC Mixed Teams\); Victoria
-   January: Regionals – UBC vs\. SFU and UBC vs\. UVIC
-   February: Whitman College, Seattle
-   March: Canadian Western Championships, UBC TSC Women’s Team vs Women’s Prairie Champions, Home

# Welcome to UBC Recreation Fitness & Classes

UBC Rec’s fitness programs are dedicated to improving the health and wellbeing of the UBC community\. Two fitness centres \(at the ARC and Rec North\) and multiple studio spaces spread across the Point Grey campus offer a variety of spaces to workout\. Additionally, Women \(Trans Women Welcome\) & Two\-Spirit, Trans, Non\-Binary \(2STNB\) fitness hours, a bouldering cave, various fitness classes, and personal training are also offered\. 

[https://recreation\.ubc\.ca/drop\-in/fitness\-classes/](https://recreation.ubc.ca/drop-in/fitness-classes/)[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/Icon-_Adult.png)

# Get to know our Personal Trainers\!

Welcome\! Thank you for wanting to know more about our team\. You can read about the story and specialization of our personal trainers by clicking on their **name** below:

---

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ChatGPT-Image-Mar-12-2026-05_36_27-PM-e1773362809283-150x150.png)

Simon

Simon is a NASM Certified Personal Trainer and a fifth\-year Kinesiology student at the University of British Columbia with over three years of coaching experience\. At UBC Recreation, he has worked with a wide range of clients including beginners, students, older adults, athletes, and individuals managing health conditions\.

Simon’s training approach focuses on building strength, improving movement quality, and developing resilience\. He tailors programs to each client’s goals, abilities, and experience level while emphasizing a strong foundation for long\-term health and performance\.

His coaching style is supportive and educational, helping clients understand their training so they can feel confident, capable, and eventually train independently\.

*Fun fact: Simon can juggle with one hand\.*

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/2026-03-12_17-11-10-e1773360718271-150x150.png)

Marshal

title: Rules & Etiquette
content_markdown:
For the enjoyment and safety of all patrons inside UBC Rec’s Fitness Centres, please adhere to the following rules and etiquette:

#### Fitness Centres Rules

-   UBC Card or UBC Recreation Card is required for entry and must be given to staff to scan\.
    -   **Only physical IDs are accepted\.** In the instance of lost UBC Card, a Government Issued ID will be temporarily accepted for entry, however confirmation must be presented that a new UBC Card has been ordered via [UBCcard Online Services\.](https://services.ubccard.ubc.ca/#:~:text=UBCcard%20is%20the%20official%20identification,Library%20and%20UBC%20Food%20Services)
    -   Please note **memberships are non transferable**, and the **use of someone else’s membership/UBC ID to access the fitness facilities is prohibited**\.
-   No food, gum, or drinks except water are permitted\. 
    -   Please use water bottles and containers with a lid\.
-   Backpacks, bags, umbrellas, skateboards, etc\. are not permitted in fitness centres\. 

#### Apparel Rules

-   No jeans or jean shorts allowed\. 
-   Proper athletic shoes and workout clothes must be worn when in the fitness centres\. 
    -   Closed toe shoes must be worn **at all times and in every area** of the fitness centres\.

#### Equipment Rules

-   Do not move equipment between floors or remove equipment from the fitness centres\.
-   Small equipment can be requested from the fitness centre desks by asking a staff member for use in exchange for an ID, and then must be returned after use\. 
-   Only use equipment on which you have been given proper instruction on\. 
-   Please report any equipment malfunctions to the staff immediately to ensure the safety of all patrons\. 

#### Proper Etiquette

-   Ask staff for assistance if you are unsure how to use a machine or piece of equipment\.
-   Use bar collars/clips on all bars at all times – please ask floor staff for them\.
-   Use of personal chalk is allowed at the Olympic platforms\.
-   Do not drop weights except on the Olympic platforms\.
-   Only bumper plates are allowed to be used on the Olympic platforms\.
-   Put away all your weights and plates after use\.
-   **Wipe down all equipment and benches before and after use to be respectful of the next person to use that piece of equipment\.**
-   Keep **your** workout area clear\.
-   Please respect time limits listed for specific areas of the fitness centres such as the free weights, stretching, and squat racks and platform areas\.
-   Do not work out between people using benches\.
-   Please limit your cardio use to 30 minutes \(20 minutes at peak times\)\.
-   If you feel faint or dizzy, stop, sit down and ask for assistance\.

*Failure to comply with these rules may result in loss of fitness centres privileges\.*

---

## Group Fitness Rules & Etiquette

### Online Reservations

Reservations open 24 hours before class time and must be made in advance\.

-   **Members** with Group Fitness access can **reserve a spot for free**\.
-   **Reservations with a paid drop\-in fee are available** if you do not have an applicable membership\.
-   If you cannot make a class, **please cancel your reservation online\.** 

### \*NEW\* Class Check\-In Procedures

To help classes run smoothly and safely,

  
✔️ **Arrive on time** for the best experience\.   
✔️ **Check in directly at the class location 5–10 minutes before class begins\.**  
❌ Once a class has started, **entry is not guaranteed\. After 5 minutes**, late arrivals will not be permitted\.

### Your team doesn’t have enough players for your next game – what do you do?

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Leagues-Flowchart_FINAL.jpg)

#### Jump To:

-   [Outcome A: Cancel your game \(in good standing\)](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/cancel-default-process/#a)
-   [Outcome B: Cancelling your game \(not in good standing\)](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/cancel-default-process/#b)
-   [Outcome C: Recruiting players prior to roster deadline](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/cancel-default-process/#c)
-   [Outcome D: Recruiting players after the roster deadline](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/cancel-default-process/#d)
-   [Outcome E: Your team had defaulted – what to do next](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/cancel-default-process/#e)

---

#### Outcome A: Cancel your game \(in good standing\)

**It is prior to the cancellation deadline and your team has not cancelled more than one game this term\.**  
Just email your League Administration \(im\.soccer@ubc\.ca, im\.basketball@ubc\.ca, etc\. which can be found on the respective league webpage\) and let them know you need to cancel your game on \[insert day\]\. Please be very specific if you have multiple games that day \(Volleyball, Dodgeball, Ultimate\) about which game\(s\) you are cancelling\.  

[Cancellation Policy: I am considering cancelling my game\. What should I know?](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/cancel-default-process/#cancellation-policy-i-am-consi-34)

##### UBC Recreation Intramural Leagues Cancellation Policy

If 3 school days or more prior notice is given by a team, the game is canceled and the requesting team records a loss \(1\-0\) and will not receive a default\.

If fewer than 3 school days’ notice is given in league play, the team is required to play\. If the team fails to show up to a game, a default is charged\.  If the team does show up, but with insufficient numbers, they may attempt to use non\-roster players to avoid defaulting\. If this occurs after the roster deadline, the team will incur a forfeit \(refer to flow chart for these specific outcomes\)\.

Teams may cancel a maximum of 2 games in a season before they are ineligible for playoffs\.

---

#### Outcome B: Cancelling your game \(not in good standing\)

**It is prior to the cancellation deadline and your team has  already cancelled one game this term\.**  
You and your team will need to decide if you want to cancel a 2nd game and thus become ineligible for playoffs \(but get to finish off your regular season\), or try and recruit extra players for that week \(See Flow Chart above or Policy below\)

Note: If you want to still be eligible for playoffs refer to the flow chart at the top of this page about how you could recruit more players\.  

[Cancellation Policy: I am considering cancelling my game\. What should I know?](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/cancel-default-process/#cancellation-policy-i-am-consi-35)

##### UBC Recreation Intramural Leagues Cancellation Policy

If fewer than 3 school days’ notice is given in league play, the team is required to play\. If the team fails to show up to a game, a default is charged\.  If the team does show up, but with insufficient numbers, they may attempt to use non\-roster players to avoid defaulting\. If this occurs after the roster deadline, the team will incur a forfeit \(refer to flow chart for these specific outcomes\)\.

Teams may cancel a maximum of 2 games in a season before they are ineligible for playoffs\.

---

#### Outcome C: Recruiting players prior to roster deadline

**You can still recruit players and add to your roster prior to the reg deadline**  
If you know you won't have enough players for your next game, but were not able to cancel your game before the cancellation deadline, you and your team mates should ask around your classes, residences, clubs, or even other teams in your league to see if anyone would be interested in being a substitute player for your game that day\.  By meeting the minimum \# of players requirements, you will be playing a fully legitimate game and you will not Default\. Who knows, you might have just found a new full\-time player fr your team as well\. Please note that all players playing for your team still need to sign in for each game for your team, regardless if they are temporary or permanent players\.  

[Number of Players Policy: How many players do I need on the field to avoid defaulting?](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/cancel-default-process/#number-of-players-policy-how-m-36)

##### UBC Recreation Intramural Leagues Minimum Number of Players Policy

Each team must field a certain number of players, also abiding by the team's respective participation structure restrictions and divisional import restrictions, in order to avoid forfeiting or defaulting\.  
The minimum number of players is different for each league:

-   11v11 Soccer \- 9
-   6v6 Soccer \- 5
-   4v4 Soccer \- 3
-   Basketball \- 4
-   Volleyball \- 5
-   Futsal \- 4
-   Dodgeball \- 5
-   Inner Tube Water Polo \- 5
-   Ice Hockey \- 5
-   Flag Football \- 4
-   Ultimate \- 6

[Eligibility Policy: Are my recruits eligible to play?](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/cancel-default-process/#eligibility-policy-are-my-recr-37)

##### UBC Intramural Programs Eligibility Policy

Participation in most Intramural events, tournaments, and leagues is restricted to current UBC staff, faculty, and students\. Proof of UBC status is required for participation in all programs\.

Intramural programs that are open to the community include Day of the LongBoat, Pumpkin Run, Lace Up for Kids, UBC Triathlon Duathlon, Storm the Wall, and the UBC Summer Soccer League\.

*Note: Students who are associated with the university but do not pay an Athletics and Recreation fee \(ELI, Affiliated Colleges\) are eligible to participate in the same manner as UBC Staff and Faculty, but must have a valid UBC ID \#\. In addition, these students must be on rosters submitted by their affiliated group to UBC Recreation Intramurals and meet the individual requirements of the affiliated group\. Please check with the administration of your affiliated group to determine requirements\.*

---

#### Outcome D: Recruiting players after the roster deadline

**To avoid defaulting your team must show up with the minimum required players, but you can forfeit the game and still be in good standing\.**  
Forfeiting a game is a much better outcome than Defaulting\.  You lose by less, and there is no loss to your Default Prevention Deposit refund\.  So even though it is after the Roster Deadline, you and your team mates should work to recruit players from your classes, residences, clubs, or even other teams in your league for your up coming game so that you meet the minimum \# of players requirement and only Forfeit and don't Default\.

[Forfeit Policy: What happens when my team forfeits?](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/cancel-default-process/#forfeit-policy-what-happens-wh-40)

##### Intramural Leagues Forfeit Policy

A forfeit occurs when a team requires the use of non\-roster players to provide the minimum number of players for a game to avoid a default\.  This can only occur after the roster deadline\. Additionally, a forfeit is applied when a CoRec team does not have meet the gender requirements\.

Forfeiting teams will record a loss for the forfeited game by the following applicable score:

-   A score of 5 – 0 for:

-   4v4 Soccer
-   Inner Tube Water Polo
-   Futsal
-   Ice Hockey
-   6v6 Soccer
-   Ultimate

-   10 – 0 for Basketball
-   3 – 0 for teams in Tier 1 Volleyball
-   2 – 0 for all other Volleyball categories
-   14 – 0 for Football
-   3 – 0 for Dodgeball and 11v11 Soccer

All teams are allowed a maximum of one forfeit during each session or term of play\. Any team receiving a second forfeit will be automatically be ineligible for playoffs\.

-   Exceptions: Double Header Leagues \(Volleyball, Ultimate, Dodgeball\)\. Your team must forfeit in different weeks to become ineligible for playoffs\. Forfeiting both games in a day will not disqualify you from playoff eligibility\.

---

#### Outcome E: Your team has defaulted \- what to do next?

If this is your first default of the season with this team, your team will be charged $25\.00 \($100\.00 for Ice Hockey\) of your Default Prevention Deposit\.  You will lose the game you defaulted by the Forfeit Policy score listed above, **but you are still in the league** and you are expected to show up to your next scheduled game\. If your team finishes the season without another default, you will still be eligible for playoffs \(if applicable\)\.  If your team defaults a second game, your team will be charged the final $25\.00 \($100\.00 for Ice Hockey\) of your Default Prevention Deposit\.  At this point, your team will be removed from the league and will receive none of your Default Prevention Deposit back or be refunded any of your registration fee\.

**New for the 2018/2019 School year is the Default Prevention Deposit\.**  Due to a rise in the number of teams defaulting each semester, we have implemented a new policy to help address this issue\.

UBC Recreation’s Fitness & Classes programs are offered across two fitness centres, a spin studio, a dojo, and several multi\-purpose studios across the UBC Vancouver campus\.

All fitness memberships include access to both ARC and Rec North Fitness Centres\.

For more information about [Fitness Centre memberships\.](https://recreation.ubc.ca/fitness-classes/memberships/)

## Rec North Fitness Centre

#### Facility Features

-   Four\-floor fitness centre
-   Olympic weightlifting & platforms
-   Personal training studio
-   Universal and gendered change facilities

#### Location

The Rec North Fitness Centre is located in the west block of the Recreation Centre North building\. There are entrances to this fitness centre located at the L0 and L2 levels of the building\. A limited quantity of short\-term lockers are available for use while visiting\.

## The ARC

#### Facility Features

-   8,000 sq\. ft of fitness centre and multi\-purpose studio space
-   Universal change room facilities
-   Personal training specific space
-   Functional training space
-   Scheduled studio drop\-in with speed and heavy punching bags

#### Location

The ARC is located in the UBC Life Building \(formerly the old Student Union Building\) on the lower and main levels of the building\. As of summer 2022, there  is ongoing construction around the Life Building, so access to the lower level \(fitness centre and change room areas\) of the ARC is most readily accessed by either the elevator in the centre of the building or the east and south stairwells\.

title: About the UBC Aquatic Centre
content_markdown:
# About the UBC Aquatic Centre

[Embedded iframe \(view source\)](https://www.youtube.com/embed/eVeygweYndw)

### Facility Features

The UBC Aquatic Centre designed for campus, community and competition services the needs of athletic training, competition, and neighbourhood leisure needs\. The new facility’s natatorium can accommodate nearly 1,000 bathers, and the viewing area in the mezzanine can host up to 460 spectators\.

#### The facility features include:

-   25 metre recreational pool with diving boards and accessible ramp
-   50 metre competition pool with Omega Swiss Timing System
-   Leisure pool and lazy river with accessible ramp
-   34\-person family friendly hot tub with accessibility lift
-   Steam room and sauna
-   Viewing decks and spectator areas
-   Men’s, women’s, and universal change rooms
-   Meeting room
-   Wet classroom

\*\*The UBC Aquatic Centre uses both chlorine and UV purification

### Amenities & Accessibility

UBC aims to be a barrier\-free, accessible environment that is respectful among all people regardless of their abilities, backgrounds, or experience\. The UBC Aquatic Centre is a fully wheelchair\-accessible space and offers plenty of amenities for it’s patrons including the following:

-   Locker rentals and swim session lockers
-   Accessible entrances with power\-operated doors
-   Accessible washrooms, change rooms, and elevators
-   Accessible ramps in the 25m recreational and leisure pools
-   Aquatic lift in the hot tub
-   Universal change room for persons with attendants
-   Braille signage
-   Food and beverage kiosk

### UBC Sustainability: Our water is blue, but our pool is green

The University of British Columbia is a global leader in sustainability\. That’s why when the plans for the new UBC Aquatic Centre were conceived, environmental sustainability was central to the final vision for a world\-class facility\. While providing leading aquatic programs and services, the new UBC pool serves as a demonstration project for water\-saving and water\-recycling strategies\. Vancouver’s temperate climate allows for millions of litres of rainwater to be collected and recycled to supply most of the water used in the building\. On any given day, up to 5 cm of water evaporates from the surface of pools\. The rainwater harvested from the building’s roof will be used to replenish water lost\. The building will save approximately 2\.7 million litres of water annually through rainwater harvesting, and almost 7,000 litres of water daily through water\-efficient showerheads\! To read “Making Waves With Sustainability at UBC Aquatic Centre” check out this [blog post](https://recreation.ubc.ca/2022/07/15/making-waves-with-sustainability-at-ubc-aquatic-centre/)\. The building is targeted to be certified LEED Gold — an achievement that shows the University as a living laboratory and agent of change\. To learn more about LEED and the sustainable features of UBC Aquatic Centre, [check out this blog post](https://recreation.ubc.ca/2022/07/15/making-waves-with-sustainability-at-ubc-aquatic-centre/)\.

---

-   [Gold Certification – Rick Hansen Foundation Accessibility Certification \(RHFAC\)](https://www.rickhansen.com/become-accessible) 
-   [Sustainability Award – Engineers and Geoscientists BC](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LzsHN6GD0AE)

-   [Global Architecture & Design Awards 2018](https://www.re-thinkingthefuture.com/gada-2018-winners/university-of-british-columbia-aquatic-centre-mjma/)

Move More, Learn More is an interactive health education program designed for women \(trans women welcome\) to learn more about health and fitness and find ways to engage with physical activity that suits their lifestyle\. From yoga, to weight training, dancing and more – come find what moves you\! Plus, participants can earn a variety of prizing for attendance\!

## Attend More, Win More\!

Move More, Learn More has an attendance based prizing initiative in which you could win the following\!

-   **Attend 7 classes and win a lululemon yoga mat\!**
-   **Attend 11 classes and win a Fitbit or lululemon belt bag\!**

---

**Ready to move more and learn more?** Register below\!

# Intramurals is Hiring\!

**Jump To:** [Current Opportunities](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/#Opportunities) \| [Leagues](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/#league) \| [Events](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/#events) \| [Media/Digital Content](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/#media) \| [Hear From Previous Staff](https://recreation.ubc.ca/2021/04/07/inside-look-to-intramurals/) \| [Questions?](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/#questions)

### Current Opportunities 

**UBC Intramurals is currently accepting applications to Volunteer Staff positions for the 2026/2027 academic year\!** Applications will close on **March 25, 2026 at 11:59PM\.**

For any inquiries, feel free to contact the Intramural Program Development team at [im\.prod@ubc\.ca](mailto:im.prod@ubc.ca)\.

---

### Who We Are

For over 50 years, Intramural staff have passionately volunteered their time and delivered some of UBC’s most iconic events, leagues, and marketing initiatives\. Supported by professional staff with experience in sport management and student development, all of our student staff are challenged to grow as individuals and innovate within their roles as student leaders while being a part of one of the most immersive student experiences on campus and recognizable Intramural staff programs in the country\.

From the thousands of staff who have spent time in this program, many have called this experience pivotal for both their time at UBC, and in their lives\. If you are looking for a work hard, play hard community on campus, Intramurals could be the place for you\.

---

### What We Do

With over a dozen departments and 100 student staff, there are many opportunities for staff to gain experience in diverse areas of programming\. The Intramural staff program consists of three involvement areas – Leagues, Events, Media, and Digital Content\. Within these areas, there are multiple teams of student staff made up of Assistant Directors \(ADs\) led by one Director\. These teams work to create a positive participant and student experience across campus\.

From organizing tournaments, races, and leagues, to engaging students through digital content and storytelling, there is something for everyone\! Keep reading below to find out more details:

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/circle-cropped-300x300.png)

**INTRAMURAL LEAGUES  
**  
[***Hiring Open \| Intramural League Staff***](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/leagues-staff/)  
The League’s team coordinates sports games for thousands of participants on just about every field, rink, and court across campus every week, through 11 different sports\. Leagues staff work closely with participants during on\-site supervisory shifts, and take on key administrative roles within their team, gaining experience in scheduling, participant experience, customer service, program management, and more\.

[**Hear From Previous League Staff**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/#hear-from-previous-league-staf-29)

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Aug-30-Zeus-214x300.jpg) *"Intramurals is everything you'd ever want out of your university experience: a wholesome family and people that support you during tough times and raise you higher after your wins\. It's a community that makes you want to be the best version of yourself and you're guaranteed to have some truly amazing experiences along the way\!"* **\- Zeus, Leagues Student Staff 2017\-2020**

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/circle-cropped-1-300x300.png)

**INTRAMURAL** **EVENTS**  
[***Hiring Open \| Intramural Volunteer Event Staff***](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/events-staff/)   
Building on a reputation for excellence that is many decades in the making, the Events team runs some of UBC's most iconic events\. From Day of the LongBoat to Storm the Wall, Intramurals student staff drive the development, planning, and delivery of a diverse portfolio of exciting events\. Staff are challenged and empowered in this professional event planning environment and will gain skills in large\-scale event management, event production & atmosphere, logistics efficiency, race management, and more\.

[**Hear From Previous** **Event Staff**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/#hear-from-previous-event-staff-30)

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/102619_GreatTrek_BDhaliwal-207-3-1.jpg)

*“The UBC Intramurals student volunteer program has been the most impactful thing that has ever happened to me\. I made some my closest friends through the program\. I learned what sort of person I wanted to be and the full\-time staff pushed me to accomplish things I never thought I could and made some of the most amazing memories I have ever lived through\.”*

**\- Timme, Events Student Staff 2018\-2022**

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/circle-cropped-4-300x300.png)

**INTRAMURAL MEDIA & DIGITAL CONTENT  
**  
[**Hiring Open \| Intramural Volunteer Media & Digital Content Staff**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/media-digital-content-staff/)  
Media& Digital Content \(Events & Leagues\) is made up of 3 teams who are responsible for creating and maintaining the Intramural brand story \- promoting participation, engagement, and recognition in all Intramural programs, using a variety of innovative strategies\. These staff help to define the role of Intramurals within the UBC community\. Media is the most unique, and technically elevated team in the Intramural program\. From videography, photography, creative content & story\-telling, to internal community building through the lens, Media sees and does it all\.

[**Hear From Previous** **Digital Content Staff**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/#hear-from-previous-digital-con-31)

These teams are focused on driving awareness and registration for all Intramural programming through the creation of innovative content for a variety of professional digital channels\. These staff will gain experience in digital strategy, creative content production, video editing, business accounts, and more\. [Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Kelly_Z-360x240.jpg) *"The experience working in the marketing of the Intramurals Leagues and Events like LongBoat and the UBC Triathlon Duathlon helped me gain insights into working professionally in digital marketing and helped me apply the skills and knowledge I had from class and previous work\. We were given so much trust and control with our projects and this really helped my team and I flourish\. It was a great opportunity to develop and further my marketing skills while creating meaningful lifelong connections and friendships\."* **\- Kelly, Digital Content & Program Development Student Staff, 2018\-2021**

[**Hear From Previous** **Media \(Photography/Videography\) Staff**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/employment/intramural-staff/#hear-from-previous-media-photo-32)

This team produces high\-quality visual imagery for both Intramural participants and staff\. Team members are encouraged to bring their own creative ideas into the team's projects\. These staff will gain experience in story\-boarding & content management, photo & video composition, coverage of large\-scale sport events & programs, editing efficiency, and more\. [Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/72346704_2604574056271411_5401297600970227712_n.jpg)

*"Being part of the Media team means getting to take photos at major UBC events such as Storm of Wall and Day of the Longboat but there’s a lot more beyond that\. The media team gets to capture the behind the scenes for the program and you bond really closely with your other media team members\."*

**\- Kana \(right\), Media Student Staff, 2018\-2021**

**The volunteer program that has impacted hundreds of thousands of participants over a decades\-long legacy of community on campus\.**

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/IMCOVER4.jpg)

## About the Team

The UBC Thunderbirds Table Tennis Sport Club is a highly competitive team competing under the National Collegiate Table Tennis Association \(NCTTA\), as well as other major tournaments locally and nationally\. Our sport club includes a co\-ed team and a women’s team\. Each competing team features 8\-10 student\-athletes\.

The club’s goal is to represent UBC locally, at the NCTTA level, and even internationally and to succeed at every level\. The season runs from September to April and we hold multiple practices each week\. In addition, we encourage participation in tournaments throughout the season to build up experience leading up to NCTTA tournaments or simply to continue growing as an athlete\.

For more information, please see the sections below or contact us at:

-   Email: [tabletennis\.sc@ubc\.ca](mailto:tabletennis.sc@ubc.ca)
-   Instagram: [@ubctabletennis](https://www.instagram.com/ubctabletennis/)
-   LinkTree: [https://linktr\.ee/ubctabletennis](https://linktr.ee/ubctabletennis)

[How to Join](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/table-tennis-sc/#how-to-join-8)

**Eligibility Requirements**

We are looking for passionate and skilled table tennis players who are excited to join a great competitive team to make a positive difference with the club\!

Expectations for team members include:

-   Attendance at mandatory practice sessions
-   Attendance at local and national tournaments
-   Be active in team events and fundraising efforts

Many of the tournaments take place in the United States so team members will have to have a valid passport and/or a US Visa or other documents that confirm your eligibility to cross the border\.

**Tryouts**

More information will be posted on our Instagram account, [@ubctabletennis](https://www.instagram.com/ubctabletennis/?hl=en), and the Facebook page, [UBC Table Tennis](https://www.facebook.com/groups/ubctabletennis/) at the beginning of September every year\.

**Team Fees**

Team fees may vary between $400\-700 and are currently under review\. This will cover some team expenses such as travel costs, gym rental, jerseys and more\. Additionally, team members are expected to contribute to and take part in fundraising efforts throughout the season\. An annual surplus of funds will be reimbursed to members on a regular basis\. Team fees are subject to change\.

**Practice Schedule**

Weekly practice typically occurs on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays in the first semester\. Schedules may change as we change semesters\. Specific times and locations for practices are to be determined\. Team members are expected to attend all practices unless there are unexpected emergencies or other valid reasons that are communicated appropriately\.

Practice schedule is subject to change\.

**Competitions**

There are four NCTTA tournaments throughout the Winter Session and all team members are expected to attend all tournaments\. The club also participates in locally\-held tournaments or other tournaments outside of the NCTTA throughout the year depending on the competition level and the schedule\.

**Academic Requirements**

Team members are required to maintain good academic standing – minimum 60% average or passing standards as identified by their faculty – and must not be on academic probation\.

Team members must be students at the University of British Columbia who are registered in an Undergraduate or Graduate 9\-credit course load per term in the current winter session, or fulfilling the requirements for a PhD/Masters, or Co\-op Program\. \(Students registered in diploma programs, certificate programs, or affiliated colleges/ programs with the University of British Columbia including: Carey Theological College, Regent College, St\. Mark’s College, and the Vancouver School of Theology, are not eligible for active membership in a UBC Thunderbirds Sport Club\.\)

[History](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs/table-tennis-sc/#history-11)

The UBC Table Tennis Club was founded in 2002 as an AMS club\. The club provided an opportunity for table tennis athletes to get together to practice, compete, and share their love for the sport\. All the while, the club continuously pushed for more recognition for the sport within the local community, the University of British Columbia, and other BC universities\. In 2006, the club developed a competitive team, providing a platform for experienced table tennis athletes to travel and compete in national and international events across Canada and the United States\.

Since then, the competitive team has actively competed in the National Collegiate Table Tennis Association\. The team achieved multiple Northwest divisional and West Regional titles, and has also consistently placed in the top 16 at the National Collegiate Table Tennis Championships\.

In 2020, the competitive team parted ways with the AMS UBC Table Tennis Club to join the UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs\. Today, the UBC Table Tennis Thunderbirds Sport Club attracts experienced table tennis student\-athletes by providing one of the few opportunities in Canada to develop advanced athletic and student leadership skills\.

title: UBC Recreation Registration System
content_markdown:
> UBC Recreation’s registration system enables:
> 
> -   Integration with UBC CWL to qualify for affiliated rates
> -   Enhanced online experience
> -   Managing additional Family Members
> 
> Since May 2020 most UBC Recreation programs and activities require an online login\. If you have not recently set up a new login, please read and follow instructions on this page\.

*For the optimal experience with the system, please use the Google Chrome browser when searching and registering for UBC Recreation programs\. The Safari browser is not compatible with a number of features and we strongly recommend using an alternate browser when using the online registration software; not all features may work as intended with other browsers\.*

### 1\. Set Up & Edit Your UBC Recreation Login

#### UBC Campus Wide Login \(CWL\)

Current UBC students, faculty, staff, and alumni can use their CWL to access the registration software\. Prior to registering for a program or visiting UBC facilities, activate your UBC Recreation Login with your CWL to verify your affiliations\. This initial login verifies your affiliations\.

[https://portal\.recreation\.ubc\.ca/sso/index\.php](https://portal.recreation.ubc.ca/sso/index.php)[CWL Login](https://portal.recreation.ubc.ca/img/CWL_login_button.png)

*UBC Students – please note that it may take up to 24 hours for your CWL to connect with your login for discounted rates and access to activities such as drop\-in sports, tennis court bookings, memberships, etc\.*

[Instructions for Setting Up Your CWL with UBC Recreation](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2020-PM-CWL-Login.pdf)

#### Public

Individuals without a UBC CWL will need to create a new login\. Creating your login online will ensure you are ready to register for programs and expedite your next visit to our facilities\.

[**Create Login**](https://portal.recreation.ubc.ca/index.php?r=public/index)

[Instructions for Setting Up a Public UBC Recreation Login](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2020-PM-Public-Login.pdf)

#### Community Services Card \(CSC\) and University Neighbourhoods Association \(UNA\)

Residents with CSC eligibility or a UNA card should follow the same steps as the public to create their login\. In\-person verification by presenting your CSC or UNA card at a [designated recreation facility](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/new-reg/#locations) will qualify you to receive the affiliated rates \(including through online registration\) for a one year period\.

[**Create Login**](https://portal.recreation.ubc.ca/index.php?r=public/index)

### 2\. Adding Family Members \(optional\)

A Family Account is used to register for programs, manage memberships, and see schedules for a family\. After setting up your UBC Recreation Login, your account will be designated as the primary contact and you can add additional Family Members\. It is recommended that where applicable, the primary login should be a family member with a UBC Campus Wide Login\. [Instructions for Adding Family Members](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2025-PM-Account-Features.pdf)

### 3\. Rate Verification for UNA & CSC and Family Member UBC Camps rates for UBC Students, Faculty, and Staff \(optional\)

Additional verification of your University affiliations is required for certain rates\. Please follow the steps outlined below to activate these rates:

#### UNA & CSC

In\-person verification by presenting your CSC or UNA card at a [designated recreation facility](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/new-reg/#locations) will qualify you to receive the affiliated rates \(including through online registration\) for a one year period\.

#### Family Member UBC Camps rates for UBC Students, Faculty, and Staff – only for UBC Camps

An [online submission](https://recreation.ubc.ca/camps/camps-rate-form/) of the University affiliated individual will qualify Family Members on the same account to receive applicable UBC Camps rates for a one year period\. Verification requests require up to three business days\.

### 4\. Register for Programs

Browse through programs on the [UBC Recreation](https://recreation.ubc.ca/) or [UBC Camps](https://camps.ubc.ca/) website\. Click on any button that features “Register Now” to use your CWL or UBC Recreation Login to complete registration\.

[Instructions for Program Registration](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2020-PM-Registration.pdf)

## Additional Information About the Registration System

[Walkthroughs of System Features](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/new-reg/#walkthrough)

[Frequently Asked Question](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/new-reg/#FAQs)

[UNA & CSC Verification Locations](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/new-reg/#locations)

### Walkthroughs

### Frequently Asked Questions

I have more than one affiliation with UBC, how will this affect my login and rates?

Individuals with with faculty, staff, and student affiliations at UBC will be verified automatically using their CWL\. If there are multiple affiliations, you will receive the lowest available rate\. For individuals that also have a UNA and CSC affiliation, once in\-person verification is completed any lower available rate will be applied for future transactions\.

Why am I receiving emails from communication@xplorrecreation\.com or info\.rec@recreation\.svc\.ubc\.ca?

Emails from the registration system are sent from one of these two email addresses\. It is not spam, please ensure that these email addresses are added to your safe list\.​  
  
By using the UBC Recreation system you are agreeing to receive mandatory communication, such as registration confirmations, pre\-program information, and administrative messages\. These communications are an integral part of UBC Recreation programs and that you are able to opt out of receiving them\.

Why did I not receive a confirmation email?

Please check your spam or junk mail folder\. Emails from the registration software will be sent from communication@xplorrecreation\.com and info\.rec@recreation\.svc\.ubc\.ca\. Please ensure that both of these email addresses are on your safe list\.

I need help\. Who do I contact?

If you require assistance with your UBC Recreation Login, program registration, or support with the registration system, please email [recreation\.help@ubc\.ca](mailto:recreation.help@ubc.ca)\.

Why is my age 120 years? Why is my phone number wrong? How do I fix it?

For CWL users, you will see a default age and phone number that may be incorrect\. Please follow these [instructions](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2025-PM-Account-Features.pdf) to update your information\.

Your account credit is still on file with us; however it cannot be transferred over to our new system\. Existing account credit can be used for tennis, ice, rowing or baseball non\-camp programs running from January to March 31, 2020\. Any unused credit will be returned to customers\.

### Online Reservations & Drop\-In Access

#### **Reserve Your Spot Online** 

Reservations open **24 hours before class time** and must be made in advance\. 

-   Have a membership that includes Group Fitness? **Book classes for free\.** 
-   No membership? No problem\! Join a class with a **[drop\-in fee](https://recreation.ubc.ca/drop-in/group-fitness/#rates)**\. 
-   Can’t make it? If you’ve reserved a spot but can’t attend, **please cancel your reservation** to free up space for others\. 

#### **New\! Class Check\-In Procedures** 

To help classes run smoothly and safely, 

✔️ **Arrive on time** for the best experience\.   
✔️ **Check in directly at the class location** **5–10 minutes before class begins**\. 

❌ Once a class has started, **entry is not guaranteed**\. After **5 minutes**, late arrivals will not be permitted\. 

### Activities

Group Fitness

From high\-energy cardio to strength training, athletic conditioning, and dance, our Group Fitness classes offer something for everyone\. Whether you want to push your limits, move to the music, or build endurance, each class is designed to challenge, energize, and inspire\. With motivating instructors and a supportive community, you’ll leave every workout feeling stronger, more confident, and more connected\.

| **Class** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **AthletiX** | Train like an athlete and move with purpose in this explosive, full\-body workout\. AthletiX combines resistance training with speed and agility drills to improve strength, coordination, and precision\. Whether you want to jump higher, run faster, or simply challenge your body in new ways, this class helps you level up your fitness game\. |
| **Barre** | Barre Fitness combines yoga, Pilates, and ballet barre conditioning to tone your whole body while developing balance, strength, and flexibility\. Classes will utilize both the mat and the ballet barre\. Required Equipment: Barre classes can be performed in shoes, socks, bare feet, or ballet slippers\. |
| **H\.I\.I\.T\.** | Maximize results in minimal time with high\-intensity interval training \(H\.I\.I\.T\.\)\. This fast\-paced, calorie\-torching workout cycles through short bursts of all\-out effort followed by brief recovery periods, skyrocketing your metabolism and building endurance\. Get ready to sweat and push past your limits\. |
| **KickFit** | KickFit gets you fit like a kickboxer – no experience required\. Led by experienced Kickboxing/Muay Thai instructors, this high\-energy class focuses on conditioning, not combat\. You’ll build cardio, core strength, and endurance through striking drills, pad work, and fight\-inspired circuits\. Whether you’re brand new or have already participated in our registered Kickboxing or Muay Thai instructional programs, KickFit is the perfect way to elevate your fitness\. |
| **Strength** | Unleash your power and build lasting strength in this results\-driven class\. We’ll sculpt lean muscle and enhance your overall fitness while lifting safely and confidently\. Whether you’re here to level up your fitness or just want to feel stronger in your daily life, this class delivers\. No experience? No problem\. Just show up, push your limits, and get ready to feel unstoppable\. |
| **Surge** | Ignite your endurance and improve your stamina in this high\-octane cardio class\. We’ll push your limits by blending heart\-pounding intervals with movements that build speed, agility and cardiovascular endurance\. Perfect for anyone wanting to break a sweat, crush goals and leave class buzzing with energy\. No experience? No problem\. Just show up, push your limits, and get ready to feel unstoppable\. |
| **Zumba** | Zumba fuses hypnotic Latin rhythms and easy\-to\-follow moves to create a unique fitness program that will blow you away\. Zumba’s choreography incorporates a wide variety of dance styles in a high energy setting\. |

Spin

Power through sprints, climbs, and intervals in our high\-energy Spin classes\. Set to motivating music and led by dynamic instructors, each ride challenges your endurance, builds cardiovascular strength, and keeps you coming back for more\. Whether you’re new to cycling or a seasoned rider, you’ll find a supportive, electrifying atmosphere that pushes you to ride stronger every time\.

| **Class** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Endurance Cycle** | Develop your muscular and cardiovascular endurance\!  This 60\-minute sweat session uses high\-energy music to motivate you through longer speed intervals and climbing drills and leaves you with a sweaty endorphin high\. |
| **Express Cycle** | Short and sweet\!  Ride the rhythm of the music through this high\-intensity Express class to maximize cardio training and calorie burn in 35\-minutes\. |
| **Power Cycle** | Improve your cardio while building muscular strength and endurance\!  This 45\-minute class is filled with energetic combinations of speed work, intervals, climbs, and high\-RPM sprints\. |

Yoga & Pilates

Strengthen your body and calm your mind with our Yoga & Pilates classes\. These mindful movement practices focus on breath, alignment, and core stability to build strength, flexibility, and balance\. Whether you’re looking to recharge, restore, or reconnect, each class offers a supportive space to move with intention and leave feeling grounded, centered, and refreshed\.

| **Class** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Flow Yoga** | Fun and appropriate for all levels of skill for yoga\. Flow Yoga places an emphasis on moving through postures while synchronizing your breath and movement, this class will develop core strength, breath awareness and improve your spine’s alignment\. |
| **Hatha Yoga** | A relaxed, revitalizing all\-levels class designed to improve flexibility and muscle tone\. Transitions between poses are slower\-paced, providing more opportunity to focus on alignment and form\. |
| **Pilates** | Pilates is designed to stretch and strengthen the muscles, creating a toned and lean look\. Pilates improves posture, flexibility and balance\. Core exercises are emphasized, and you will definitely feel the burn\! |
| **Vinyasa Yoga** | Vinyasa Yoga focuses on strength, endurance, balance and flexibility\. Practitioners flow through yoga postures like sun salutations while maintaining mindfulness and connection to the breath\. |

content_markdown:
The DMTSC is excited to offer a wide\-range of private lessons for hockey, figure skating and skating both on and off the ice\!  We offer private and semi\-private training for youth and adults with our main purpose to work on your desired developmental needs\. Each lesson is one hour in length\.

> **COVID\-19 Change:** During the initial reopening phase of the facility, Off\-Ice Private Lessons on a one\-on\-one instruction will only be permitted\. Groups of up to 4 will be permitted where the participants are from the same household\.

### How to Book a Private Lesson

1.  Persons interested in private lessons will be required to register online using their new UBC Recreation login\. If you have not previously registered in a program this year or in a 2020 spring break or summer camp, you will need to set up a new online login\. 

[**Create a UBC Recreation Login**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/home/new-reg/) 

2.  Purchase a 5\-lesson package\. You will use this package to register in each individual private lesson\. Please note that you will not be able to register in a lesson without purchasing this package\. 

[**Purchase a Private Lesson Package**](https://ubc.perfectmind.com/24063/Client/MembershipWidget/List?widgetId=de4a6e96-19a4-4104-9941-f612570b7513) 

3.  Using your package, register in any of the available private lesson times\.

[**Book a Private Lesson**](https://ubc.perfectmind.com/24063/Clients/BookMe4BookingPages/Classes?calendarId=a7fc390c-736c-44a2-a1ce-e58af5f9b404&widgetId=15f6af07-39c5-473e-b053-96653f77a406&embed=False) 

-   -   An Instructor will be in touch directly to confirm the lesson\. If you have any questions prior to the lesson, please contact: [hockey\.programs@ubc\.ca](mailto:hockey.programs@ubc.ca)\. 
    -   We understand it is likely you will build a rapport with your instructor\. After a membership is purchased and a few lessons are booked online, you may connect directly with them to book time that may not be listed online\. You can connect with our Instructors through email\.

##### Please Note:

-   Lessons must be booked three days in advance\.
-   Once you have completed 5 private lessons, you will be required to purchase another 5\-pass membership if you wish to continue\.
-   Off\-Ice Hockey Lessons will take place on our Off\-Ice shooting range and dry\-floor space\. Lessons will be tailored to your individual needs\.

### Contact Us

If you have any questions about Private Lessons, please email [hockey\.programs@ubc\.ca\.](mailto:hockey.programs@ubc.ca)

### What To Expect

> **COVID\-19 Change:** At the moment, we are only offering Off\-Ice Hockey Stickhandling and Shooting Private Lessons\. For more information on the changes and safety measures being implemented, head to our DMTSC Return To Activity page [here](https://recreation.ubc.ca/covid-updates/ice-covid/)\.

content_markdown:
[Embedded content: About the UBC Thunderbirds](https://recreation.ubc.ca/get-moving/first-year/)[Media source](https://www.dropbox.com/s/tnh4k2ipc5kvj3p/AR-FYE_final2020.mp4?raw=1)

First Year Experience

Welcome to the UBC Thunderbirds family\! UBC Athletics & Recreation is an exciting part of your university experience – we offer exceptional opportunities that help you be your best while at university, build friendships and feel connected to the UBC community\.

## Beginning Your Athletics & Recreation Experience

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/studentgym-360x164.jpg)

### Reach your full potential at school

A little physical activity can go a long way at school\! From reduced stress and anxiety, to better cognitive performance and increased productivity, as well as improved mood, UBC Recreation aims to help you reach be your best while on campus\.

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/friendsatubc.jpg)

### Make friendships and build a community

Students who participate in recreation programs at UBC are more likely to report that they have supportive friendships and a sense of belonging at UBC\. Taking a break from studying to enjoy some fresh air or physical activity with friends or classmates can make a world of a difference for your student experience\.

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/studentswim.jpg)

### Challenge yourself and try something new

Picking up a new hobby or activity can be intimidating or daunting, but there are plenty of affordable and fun opportunities to learn new sports or activities at UBC\.

[Top picks to help you **Reach Your Full Potential**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/get-moving/first-year/#top-picks-to-help-you-reach-yo-54)

##### [Fitness Centre Memberships:](https://recreation.sites.olt.ubc.ca/fitness-classes/fitness-memberships/)

One affordable membership gives you unlimited access to two fitness centres on campus\. Round out your weekly workouts by adding on memberships for Yoga & Pilates and Spin & Group Fitness classes to help you fit activity into your day\.

##### [Free Drop\-In Sports at the SRC:](https://recreation.ubc.ca/drop-in/drop-in-sports-schedule/)

The SRC offers a variety of drop\-in sports \(from badminton, to futsal, to table tennis\) that UBC Students can attend for free with a valid UBC card\.

##### [Aqua Fitness Classes:](https://recreation.ubc.ca/drop-in/aquatic-centre-schedule/)

Increase your physical activity, flexibility, and have fun in a low\-impact setting\. Drop\-In Aqua Fitness classes are free to attend with a valid Student ID card, plus you can relax afterwards in the hot tub, steam room, or sauna – does it get much better than that?

[Top picks to **Make Friendships and Build a Community at UBC**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/get-moving/first-year/#top-picks-to-make-friendships--55)

##### [Intramural Leagues & Events:](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals)

UBC Recreation hosts numerous iconic events throughout the school year at varying levels of competition and it offers 10 different league sports throughout the school year in addition to a summer soccer league\. While league sports and iconic events like Day of the LongBoat are on hiatus this fall, there's a new mix of online and in\-person programs to choose from\. These activities are designed to keep you connected to the UBC community whether you're in another country or nearby\.

##### [UBC Thunderbirds Sport Clubs:](https://recreation.ubc.ca/sport-clubs)

UBC TSC is a competitive sport option on campus that is for students, by students\. This program offers opportunities for highly competitive students to officially represent the university in sports at the non\-varsity level, to build community, and to gain leadership and sport management skills\. If you trained in one of the available sports in high school, or are looking to diversify your athletic skillset this may be the community for you\.

[Top picks to **Challenge Yourself and Try Something New**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/get-moving/first-year/#top-picks-to-challenge-yoursel-56)

##### Learn to Play Tennis:

Learn to play tennis with Adult 1\.0 Clinics\! These programs focus on the fundamentals and basics of tennis and include 4 or 5 weeks of coaching\. From there you can progress to further levels of singles clinics or drills, or take an Intro to Doubles clinic\! UBC Students get a discount on all programs, and you can also practice your skills with court booking discounts\!

##### Learn to Swim:

Did you know that UBC Recreation offers a variety of swim lessons designed for students? For beginners, you can learn the life skill of swimming for just $3 per lesson for 8 sessions, the swim instructors will show you the basics of moving through the water\!

##### Learn to Skate:

Want to learn Canada’s sport? Start with skating basics at the Doug Mitchell Thunderbird Sports Centre\. Our friendly and knowledgeable instructors will teach you skating and stopping basics so you can hop on the ice with your friends\!

[The Complete List of **Discounts Available to UBC Students**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/get-moving/first-year/#the-complete-list-of-discounts-57)

Please note all of these discounts are available to UBC Students when they have paid their A&R Fee with their student fees, and when they present a valid Student ID card\.

##### Facility Membership & Drop\-In Fees:

-   Free drop\-in swimming at the UBC Aquatic Centre during public swim times
    -   Includes free access to Drop\-In Aqua Fitness Classes
    -   Discounts on Specialty Drop\-In Aqua Fitness Classes
    -   $3 Student Swim Lessons for Beginners
    -   Discounts on Adult Lessons
    -   Discounts on Advanced Programs, Certifications, and other Adult Aquatics Programs
-   Free drop\-in public skating at the Doug Mitchell Thunderbird Sports Centre \- limited for Fall 2020 due to COVID\-19

    -   Discounts on skate rentals
    -   Discounts on Learn to Skate & Hockey Programs
-   Discounted $40 fitness centre memberships at the BirdCoop & ARC
    -   Discounts on fitness classes, boot camps, dance classes, martial arts classes, as well as yoga and Pilates classes
    -   Discounts on personal training packages
-   Free drop\-in sports at the Student Recreation Centre and ARC
-   Discounts on adult programs at the UBC Tennis Centre
    -   Student Drills Sessions are a dedicated program just for UBC Students to take their tennis game to the next level during the lunch hour
    -   Discounted Court Bookings

---

## Learn More

Joining us for Athletics & Recreation’s First Week? Curious about getting involved? Looking for more information on our programs? Here are some great resources to help start your adventure with UBC Recreation\.

#### Find Your Rec

[Header image showing UBC's south sport facilities](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/23134863229_6a28cb303d_o-940x196.jpg)

Answer a few short questions to get some customized recommendations and programs to try\!

#### Facilities

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/MicrosoftTeams-image-11-scaled.jpg)

Take a virtual tour of UBC’s Sport Facilities and see what’s offered at each location\.

[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Students-Relaxing-in-the-Hot-Tub-UBC-Aquatic-Centre-1.jpg)

A quick guide to a few terms you might hear or read around UBC Rec’s programs & facilities\.

[**Let’s Dive In**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/2021/08/26/recreation-terms/)

---

## Join an Intramural Team

If you’re looking to meet other first year students, registering for one of the First Year Experience Intramural teams is a great way to connect with new people\. When you sign up for one of these teams, you’ll be placed on a team with other new\-to\-UBC students and play weekly games in one of UBC Recreation’s intramural leagues\.

> Interested in setting up your own team? Be sure to check out UBC Recreation’s 10 intramural leagues to find out more information about registration and key dates\.
> 
> [**More Info About Intramural Leagues**](https://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/leagues)

---

## Free Programs & Activities

Whether you’re on campus or at home this year, you’ll find a variety of programs and activities that are exclusive to you as a First Year student\! From free online fitness classes, T\-Birds Game Nights, an immersive virtual escape room experience during Jump Start, and many opportunities to win amazing prizes, get involved with UBC Athletics & Recreation for an awesome First Year Experience\!

[https://move\.ubc\.ca/](https://move.ubc.ca/)[Image](https://recreation.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/FYE-Move-UBC-Square.jpg)

Move UBC is a university\-wide annual initiative to increase physical activity and reduce the time students, staff, faculty and the UBC community spend sitting\. Small changes can add up to big impacts—moving more and sitting less can improve both mental and physical health, impact academic and professional success, and contribute to wellbeing in meaningful ways\.

title: Welcome to Free Week
content_markdown:
### Monday, September 14 – Sunday, September 20, 2026

Welcome to UBC Recreation’s Free Week – a week when you can try out a variety of fitness classes for free\! Open to UBC Students, UBC Faculty & Staff, and the public, programs are available across several recreation facilities at UBC Vancouver’s Point Grey campus\. No experience is required for any of the classes and all abilities are welcome\! Please note Free Week is only available to to registered fitness classes and group fitness\.

### How to Participate:

-   **A FREE reservation is required\.**
-   Reservations are available 24 hours prior to the scheduled start time of each class\.
-   Use your online [UBC Recreation Login](https://recreation.ubc.ca/new-reg "https://recreation.ubc.ca/new-reg") to sign\-up\.
-   Please arrive at the class location 5 – 15 minutes before the start time to check\-in and claim your spot\.
    -   Note: 5 minutes prior to class start time any unclaimed spots will be given to walk\-ins who are on the waitlist\.

**If the class you want to attend is full, please sign up for the waitlist and stop by the class as any unclaimed spots will become available 5 minutes prior to the class start time\.**

### Program Types:

**After Free Week,** these programs are available through registration, memberships, or drop\-in:

-   **Registration Based Classes:** [Martial Arts](https://recreation.ubc.ca/fitness-classes/martial-arts/) and [Fundamentals of Fitness](https://recreation.ubc.ca/fitness-classes/cardio-conditioning-strength/) activities are offered as term\-long programs that require registration\.
-   **Group Fitness Classes:** [Group Fitness, Yoga & Pilates, and Spin classes](https://recreation.ubc.ca/drop-in/fitness-classes/) are included in select [Fitness Centre Memberships,](https://recreation.ubc.ca/fitness-classes/memberships/) and operate on a drop\-in basis\.
-   **\*NEW\* Dance Pass Classes**: All of the dance classes are available through paid drop\-in or as part of our all access pass for the term\.

***Please note that the schedules are subject to change** due to unexpected circumstances and we encourage you to bookmark and reference this schedule prior to any visit\. In the event of an unscheduled closure this calendar is the first place that we update\.*

### Online Reservations & Drop\-In Access

Some activities are available for reservations using the online registration system\. These sessions help ensure entry to visitors during peak periods\.

-   **REGISTER – Online registration is required\.**  If capacity permits walk\-in guests are welcome but are required to have a UBC Recreation account created prior to attending\. Reservations are available up to 50 hours prior to each session’s start time\. Swimmers should not arrive more than 10 minutes before the scheduled swim time\.
-   **DROP\-IN** – Entry starts at the time of the swim session, and is first\-come, first\-serve and subject to capacity\. Please ensure you have your UBC Recreation account created before your visit\.

### Facilities & Amenities

The UBC Aquatic Centre has three separate tanks that can accommodate a variety of programming options:

**Tanks:**

-   **Leisure Pool:** Accessible via stairs or a ramp with a temperature of 89\-90°F \(31\-32°C\)\. Depth ranges from 0\.9m to 1\.22m\. 
-   **Recreation Pool:** A 25m\-length pool accessible via ramp with a temperature of 80\-82°F \(26\-28°C\)\. Depth ranges from 1\.07m – 4\.5m\. 
-   **Competition Pool:** A 50m\-length by 25m\-wide tank with 1m movable bulkhead with a temperature of 78\-80°F \(26\-27°C\)\. Facilitated lift access is available upon request\. Depth is 2\.4\-2\.5m\.

**Amenities**

*Guests are advised that the following amenities may or may not be open during their visit\. Please consult the [facility schedule](https://recreation.ubc.ca/aquatics/schedule/) or contact the UBC Aquatic Centre to confirm if they are open\.* 

-   **Hot Tub:** The 34\-person capacity tank is 102\-104°F \(39\-40°C\)\.
-   **Steam Room:** Located next to the competition tank, and set to 105°F \(40\.6°C\)\.
-   **Sauna:** Located next to the competition tank, and set to 185°F \(85°C\)\.

[Click here](https://recreation.ubc.ca/aquatics/about/) for additional information on amenities at the UBC Aquatic Centre\.

### Activities

-   **Length Swim**: Sessions are suitable for lap swimming only and offered in either 50m or 25m length sessions\. Swimmers must be 13 years or older and should be comfortable in deep water\.
-   **Community Swim:** Sessions are open to all ages and abilities\.
    -   Children aged 7 and under must be accompanied by a participating adult or youth \(at least 16 years of age\) responsible for the direct supervision of the child and actively swimming within arm’s reach at all times\.
    -   Children 12 and under must be with a participating adult or youth \(at least 16 years of age\) responsible for the direct supervision of the child and actively participating in a swim session in the facility\.
    -   Please note, a participating adult is defined as an adult who is swimming in the facility\.  
-   **Training Swim:** Sessions are for swimmers comfortable in fast or express swim lanes only\. Swimmers must be 16 years or older\. Offered in either 50m or 25m length sessions\.
-   **Shallow/Deep Aquafit:** Swimmers 13 years or older who are comfortable in deep water are welcome to participate in Shallow/Deep Aquafit classes\.
-   **Hydro Board:** These aqua fitness classes are performed on floating, fitness\-specific stand\-up boards\. Energizing and fun for all skill levels\. Work on your balance, strength, core, and enjoy a fun workout\! 

*Some sessions are restricted to specific groups or members and are identified as:*

-   **UBC Student Access:** Session is available only for current UBC Students\.
-   **Toonie Swim UBC Faculty & Staff:** Session is available only to UBC Faculty & Staff at a discounted $2 rate\.
-   **Sensory Sensitive Drop\-in Swim:** sensory sensitive swim is open to all ages and abilities\. This session will have blinds lowered on the south side of the building, reduced capacities, length and open swim space available\. There will be no PA announcements, whistles or music during this time\. Guests are invited to arrive at the start time of the session\. Early entries will not be permitted\. 
-   **Two\-Spirit, Trans, Non\-Binary \(2STNB\)** **Swim Time:** Is for all who identify as two\-spirit, trans and non\-binary of all ages and swimming ability\. The Competition 50m pool and Leisure pool will be available during this session for lane and open swim\. This session will have blinds lowered on the south side of the building\. Guests are invited to arrive at the start time of the session\. Early entries will not be permitted\. 

### Drop\-in Rates & Memberships

All UBC Aquatic Centre memberships include access to aqua fitness classes and the UBC Aquatic Centre swim sessions\. [Click here](https://recreation.ubc.ca/aquatics/memberships/) for more detailed information on memberships and passes\. Guests are also welcome to purchase a drop\-in pass in\-person for drop\-in swim sessions or online for pre\-registered sessions\.
